title: China-Pakistan Nexus: Concerns Over Alleged Support to Terrorist Groups Against India
author: Lobsang Tenchoe
content: Front Slider News World 27th December 2023 27th December 2023 Lobsang Tenchoe 10028 Views 0 Comments By Tsering Choephel DHARAMSALA, 27 Dec: The Chinese Communist Party (CCP) is reportedly resurrecting its collaboration with Pakistan to support terrorist groups, exert pressure on New Delhi and redirect India-deployed army troops from the Ladakh border to the Kashmir region, as per an Intelligence Agency report cited by India Today on Tuesday. Terrorist organisations of Pakistan, such as Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) and Lashkar-e-Taiba LeT), reportedly use Chinese weapons, bodysuit cameras, and communication devices to carry out attacks on the Indian Army in the Jammu and Kashmir state. The CCP’s supply of arms and tools to these terrorist groups also includes drones, hand grenades, body cameras, guns, and sophisticated encrypted messaging devices, as outlined in the report. Furthermore, it is reported that China is aiding Pakistan in enhancing its cyber capabilities, including providing funds for the establishment of a separate information security lab dedicated to cyber warfare. In the aftermath of the consequential clash between Indian and Chinese soldiers at Galwan Valley in 2020 and the subsequent standoff, both countries have engaged in extensive strategic development and investment along the eastern front of the Indo-China border. A report from India Today on 22 December highlights India’s deployment of the Rashtriya Rifles, a specialised counter-insurgency force, from Poonch in Kashmir to Ladakh in 2020 to counter China’s aggression on the eastern front. However, this move potentially left Poonch with fewer anti-terror resources. On 21 December, heavily armed terrorists ambushed two Indian Army vehicles in the Poonch district of Jammu and Kashmir, killing four soldiers. The People’s Anti-Fascist Front (PAFF), an offshoot of the Pakistan-based terror outfit Let, claimed responsibility for the ambush. In November of this year, an Indian soldier on the Jammu border was shot, and the sniper gun used in the attack was found to be made with Chinese technology, according to the report. According to several reports, China accounts for 72% of Pakistan’s arms and weapon suppliers between 2017 and 2021. The Pakistan government allegedly makes these weapons available to terrorist organisations in Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir (POK) for infiltrations and terrorist attacks in India.

title: Nomads at the Frontline: Video Reveals Ladakhis Clashing with PLA on Disputed Border
author: Lobsang Tenchoe
content: Front Slider News World 1st February 2024 1st February 2024 Lobsang Tenchoe 7439 Views 0 Comments By Tsering Choephel A screenshot of the confrontation between herders and PLA soldiers. DHARAMSALA, 1 Feb: A video widely circulating on social media shows Ladakhi nomads in a confrontation with several Chinese armies equipped with armoured vehicles. According to media reports, the incident occurred on January 2 in the Kakjung area of the Nyoma constituency, adjacent to the Chushul Valley in Ladakh close to China-occupied Tibet near the long-contested border between India and China— known as the Line of Actual Control (LAC). The nomads, grazing their herds, were halted by patrolling People’s Liberation Army (PLA) units at LAC Patrolling Points 35 and 36. The LAC, a 3,388 km long border divided into eastern, middle, and western sectors, remains contested between India and China. Konchok Stanzin, the Chushul Councillor, stated to The Wire, “Livelihoods of locals have been taken away in the name of buffer zones and patrolling points. Our nomads are struggling for their land.” Before China invaded Tibet, Changpas, a Ladakhi nomadic tribe freely roamed the vast expanse of Changthang, part of which is in Indian territory. However, their movement has faced further restrictions due to rising border tensions and increasing PLA transgression into Indian territory. In the video, a herder can be seen shouting at a group of PLA soldiers, “Why have you come here? Why have you brought your vehicles here? This is our ancestral land; we graze our livestock here.” Stanzin, in his post accompanying the video, stated, “See how our local people are showing their bravery in front of the PLA, claiming that the area they are stopping is our nomad’s grazing land. PLA is stopping our nomads from grazing in our territory. It seems to be a never-ending process due to different lines of perceptions.” Source: India Today. The LAC, particularly the western sector in Ladakh, is most susceptible to China’s incursion strategy known as ‘salami-slicing,’ employing divide-and-rule tactics to encroach on land. Bilateral relations between the two Asian giants plummeted following the 2020 clash in the Galwan Valley, resulting in the deaths of 20 Indian soldiers and four Chinese soldiers, according to Chinese official data. As per media reports, several other skirmishes between Indian and Chinese troops along the LAC were recently revealed, with two incidents reported between September 2021 and November 2022. Despite numerous high-level dialogues, no consensus has been reached on the long-standing border dispute, and military tensions persist in border areas. The incident captured in the latest video is not a new occurrence. Several similar cases of PLA troops intercepting Indian herders from grazing have been reported, highlighting the region’s sensitivity to border friction. The Indian government’s denial of territorial loss along the LAC to China’s incursion, especially after the 2020 clash, is questioned by several reports. A ground report by VICE in the same year stated that multiple sources, including councillors and nomads, complained that China sends its nomads into Indian areas, followed by the construction of roads, helipads, and other infrastructure. Ladakhi nomads are reportedly restrained from herding near the LAC by Indian authorities as a precaution to avoid conflict with the PLA. Sonam Tsering, a local in the region, stated, “The Indian government should take the nomads into confidence. The army and paramilitary forces deployed at the post do their duty and move on, but the nomads stay. They are the real guardians of the border.” With China’s massive military buildup along the border from the Tibetan side becoming explicitly threatening, India has also increased its investment in border defence in recent years along the western sector in Ladakh and the eastern sector, where China claims the Indian state of Arunachal Pradesh as its own. India’s External Affairs Minister, S Jaishankar, has previously stated, “We have maintained our position that if China disturbs the peace and tranquility in border areas, it will impact our relations. Our relationship is not normal; it cannot be normal as the border situation is not normal.” China’s Ministry of National Defence spokesperson, Wu Qian, recently criticised India’s stand, saying, “It is unwise and inappropriate for the Indian side to insist on linking the border situation with bilateral relations,” downplaying the ‘border dispute’ with India as a ‘legacy issue.’

title: TCHRD Report: CCP’s Transnational Repression Endangers Tibetan Diaspora, Freedom Movement
author: Lobsang Tenchoe
content: Exile Front Slider News 7th February 2024 7th February 2024 Lobsang Tenchoe 7896 Views 0 Comments TCHRD Report declares Chinese Transnational Repression spreading fear and disempowering exiled Tibetans. Image: TCHRD DHARAMSALA, 7 Feb: Shedding light on the systematic repression faced by exiled Tibetan communities worldwide, the Tibetan Centre for Human Rights and Democracy (TCHRD) unveiled a groundbreaking report titled ‘Chinese Transnational Repression of Tibetan Diaspora Communities’. Released on Tuesday at the Press Club of India in the Indian capital, the report, ‘Chinese Transnational Repression of Tibetan Diaspora 2024’, exposes the insidious tactics employed by the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) to silence dissent among Tibetan exiles. Transnational repression, a term elucidated in the report, refers to the phenomenon whereby “governments reach across national borders to silence dissent among their diaspora and exile communities.” Despite widespread attention to similar phenomena, the Tibetan experience has often been obscured, overshadowed by its normalised presence within the lives of the victims. “Much has been reported about the experiences of communities targeted by the CCP transnational repression campaign, but little is known about the Tibetan experience. Until now, transnational repression against Tibetans has remained an under-acknowledged phenomenon – primarily due to its persistence, which seems to have normalised it in the lives of the victims,” TCHRD said in its first report of its kind to focus substantially on the global transnational repression of Tibetans. TCHRD highlighted a concerning pattern, exposing how Chinese authorities manipulate and intimidate Tibetans residing in Tibet to wield control over their exiled relatives. This strategy, combined with extensive surveillance efforts, fosters an environment of apprehension and suspicion within diaspora communities, heightening the peril of transnational repression for Tibetan diaspora groups and, consequently, the future of the Tibetan freedom movement. Among the documented forms of repression in the 32-page report are the severing of communication channels between exiled Tibetans and their relatives in Tibet, extensive spying to gather personal information, and coercive measures aimed at controlling behaviour abroad. Additionally, measures to undermine the livelihoods and mental well-being of exiled Tibetans are deployed, posing significant threats to their resilience and cultural ties. Ms Tenzin Dawa, Executive Director of TCHRD, issued a compelling call for action, urging democratic governments “to provide concrete protections to specific populations, including Tibetan diaspora communities that experience persecution and are targeted for transnational repression.” She emphasised, “We appeal to all democratic governments to protect human rights on their soil, through their own domestic agencies as well as creating awareness about transnational repression among various law enforcement agencies. Concrete actions such as targeted sanctions and travel bans must be imposed on individuals or government officials responsible for perpetrating acts of transnational repression.” The report stated that the CCP is pursuing a comprehensive strategy aimed at eroding Tibetan identity across all aspects, including language and religion. This approach involves utilising transnational repression, which can be viewed as a form of “sharp power” intended to infiltrate the political and cultural landscapes of targeted nations. And this, the Dharamsala-based rights group says, is being done by the CCP “to undermine the legitimacy of overseas advocacy organisations and hinder their functionality by systematically employing economic, political, or other devious means to dismantle their solidarity networks, perceived as threats to state authority, by often falsely framing them in front of the international community as enemies of the CCP intending to mislead the international community and consequently garner international support for CCP policies.

title: Former MP Jigmey Jugney Appointed Dalai Lama’s Representative at Delhi Bureau
author: Lobsang Tenchoe
content: Exile Front Slider News 30th January 2024 30th January 2024 Lobsang Tenchoe 6692 Views 0 Comments By Tsering Choephel Former parliamentarian Jigmey Jugney, the new Representative of His Holiness the Dalai Lama at the Bureau office in New Delhi. DHARAMSALA, 30 Jan: Former member of the Tibetan Parliament in exile, Jigmey Jugney, has been appointed the Representative of His Holiness the Dalai Lama at the Bureau office in New Delhi, as announced by the Kashag in a circular dated 25 January. As the key Tibetan official in the Indian capital, he will assume the responsibility of representing the Central Tibetan Administration (CTA) as the nodal officer of His Holiness the Dalai Lama and the CTA. Jugney’s appointment to the post came after his predecessor, Lobsang Shastri, who took office on 16 January 2023, resigned due to health issues recently. The appointment is effective immediately, and Jugney is the nineteenth person to hold the office. As the Representative of His Holiness the Dalai Lama at the Bureau office in New Delhi, Jugney is responsible for maintaining liaison relations with the Government of India, foreign embassies, consulates, NGOs, and civil society groups, assisting with documentation for travel-related paperwork for exile Tibetans, among other tasks. Jugney, 75, began his civil service in the Tibetan administration in 1983 as a secretary at the Tibetan Cooperative Society in Dhondeling Tibetan settlement in Kollegal, Karnataka. Later, he served as the settlement officer of Rabgyeling Tibetan settlement in Hunsur, as well as the Chief Representative Officer in Bangalore, overseeing Tibetans living in the whole of South India. In 1995, Jugney took on a secretarial role at the Department of Home and became the Secretary of the Office of the Auditor General. In 2011, he secured a seat in the Tibetan Parliament as a U-Tsang representative in the 15th Tibetan Parliament.

title: Historic Collaboration: Karmapas Unite for Shamar Rinpoche’s Recognition
author: Lobsang Tenchoe
content: Exile Front Slider News 4th December 2023 5th December 2023 Lobsang Tenchoe 10625 Views 0 Comments The Karmapas, Trinley Thaye Dorje and Ogyen Trinley Dorje pictured with the joint statement. Image: kagyuoffice.org DHARAMSALA, 4 Dec: In a significant development for the Karma Kagyu lineage of Tibetan Buddhism, the two main claimants to the title of the 17th Karmapa, the head of Tibetan Buddhism’s Kagyu lineage, Karmapa Ogyen Trinley Dorje, and Karmapa Trinley Thaye Dorje, have issued a joint statement outlining their shared responsibility for the recognition and education of the reincarnation of Kunzig Shamar Rinpoche. The tradition of recognizing tulkus, spiritual teachers’ reincarnations, is integral to Tibetan Buddhism, notably in the Karma Kagyu lineage. The joint statement emphasizes the historical significance of Shamar Rinpoche’s lineage and the need for unity after disputes following the passing of the Sixteenth Karmapa and Kunzig Shamar Rinpoche. This announcement comes after a hiatus of 170 years during which the recognition and enthronement of Shamarpa incarnations were prohibited. The Karmapas, Ogyen Trinley Dorje and Trinley Thaye Dorje, have met several times despite many difficulties, engaging in deep conversations. The Karmapas state in the joint statement that the 170-year hiatus “was a great loss to the teachings and left an irreparable hole in our history.” Key points of the joint commitment, a crucial step in maintaining the Karma Kagyu lineage’s unity and continuity, include: Collaborative Recognition: Both leaders will jointly recognize Shamar Rinpoche’s reincarnation. Shared Responsibility: Thaye Dorje and Ogyen Trinley Dorje will collectively oversee the education and spiritual guidance of Shamar Rinpoche’s Yangsi (reincarnation). Non-Interference: The process will be safeguarded from external interference to ensure authenticity. The statement concludes with a plea for unity among Karma Kagyu followers, urging sincere commitment to the Practice Lineage and discouraging disputes over reincarnations. The leaders advocate for a collective resolve to uphold the lineage’s integrity. In their efforts to unite to work together to preserve and strengthen the Kagyu lineage, the Karmapas, Ogyen Trinley Dorje and Trinley Thaye Dorje, met for the first time in 2018 at a rural location in France to get to know each other personally and held discussions on how they might collaborate to preserve and strengthen the Karma Kagyu lineage of Tibetan Buddhism. During the 37th Kagyu Monlam in Bodh Gaya in 2020, Karmapa Ogyen Trinley Dorjee made a groundbreaking announcement, marking the first instance where he stressed the significance of the two claimants to the Karmapa title, including himself and Karmapa Thaye Dorje, collaborating in the joint search for the reincarnation of Shamar Rinpoche.

title: TCHRD Director Calls Chinese Civil Society’s Open Letter to UNHRC Sign of China’s ‘Deep-Seated Insecurity’
author: Lobsang Tenchoe
content: Exile Front Slider News 29th January 2024 29th January 2024 Lobsang Tenchoe 6639 Views 0 Comments By Tsering Choephel The UN Human Rights Council in Geneva, Switzerland. Image: Fabrice COFFRINI / AFP DHARAMSALA, 29 Jan: The Tibetan Centre for Human Rights and Democracy (TCHRD) has called on the Chinese government to substantiate its accusations by addressing “the outstanding requests made by UN special procedures to investigate the actual human rights conditions on the ground.” Ms Tenzin Dawa, TCHRD’s executive director, made the remarks after a group of 73 so-called civil society organisations from China accused the International Federation for Human Rights, International Campaign for Tibet (ICT), and TCHRD of “using the platform of the Human Rights Council to spread false information and cause trouble on a large scale, with the purpose of attacking and smearing China,” in an open letter to the President of the United Nations Human Rights Council (UNHRC). The letter, published a day after 20 United Nations member states highlighted China’s abuse of human rights in Tibet during the Universal Periodic Review (UPR) of China on 23 January, charged the rights groups with fabricating lies. It listed “colonial boarding school system,” “repression of Tibetan Buddhism,” “systematic attacks on the Tibetan language,” “limitation of the rights to freedom of opinion and expression and freedom of peaceful association and assembly,” “denial of the legal rights of detainees and prisoners,” and “torture and other forms of ill-treatment” as untrue. The TCHRD director told Tibet Express that the Dharamsala-based rights group sees this letter as a reflection of China’s “deep-seated insecurity, particularly following scrutiny from more than 20 countries regarding its human rights record.” Vowing to remain steadfast and committed to advocating for the rights of Tibetans silenced under China’s rule, Dawa reflects that such a reaction from China exposes its sensitivity to its image on the international stage. She said, “The international community must continue to hold China accountable for its human rights atrocities.” The rights groups targeted in the letter, such as ICT and TCHRD, are among many independent organisations that dedicate significant resources and time to their research, campaigns, and lobbying activities in efforts to garner international attention and influence policies in dealing with the Chinese Communist government. Their numerous reports on China’s abuse of human rights inside Tibet offer a rare insight and information into what Freedom House identified as ‘the least free country.’ TCHRD Director also said that if the reports of China’s human rights abuse in Tibet in many forms are fabricated lies, as the letter accused, “China should extend invitations to human rights defenders to participate in the UN Universal Periodic Review.” Kai, the Head of UN Advocacy at ICT, said that ICT currently has no comments on the development. A report by Sophie Richardson, the Former China Director at Human Rights Watch, and Rana Siu Inboden, a Senior Fellow with the Robert Strauss Centre for International Security and Law at the UNiversity of Texas-Austin in China File on 22 January highlights China’s manipulation of the UPR process to its advantage. From a complete avoidance of talking about any of the grave human rights violations raised through other UN reviews or international civil society groups in their national report to prohibiting independent civil society in the country from participating in drafting the report, China pools all efforts into neutering the UN criticism of its rights violations. The report also highlights that “the organisations listed as contributing to the 2024 UPR national report are all either organised by or uncritical of the government.” According to a Reuters report, China lobbied non-Western countries ahead of the UPR to fill up their allotted speaking time with praise for its human rights records. A China Digital Times report on January 26 revealed China’s tactics in gathering support at the UPR using states affiliated with China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). Among the 161 states that made statements at China’s UPR session, 128 have participated in the BRI. Their report’s analysis shows that 102 BRI-subscribed states gave supportive or neutral responses to the scrutiny of China’s human rights records. China explores all avenues outside and mechanisms within the UPR to distort facts to its advantage. Many experts express concern and fear about how China is using its pressure and power to slowly change even the set principles of the UN and narratives of human rights. As such, China also targets independent rights groups directly and indirectly, here through the so-called civil society organisations.

title: Chinese Authorities Intensify Crackdown on Tibetan Children’s Education and Religious Freedom Over Winter Break
author: Lobsang Tenchoe
content: Front Slider News Tibet 10th January 2024 10th January 2024 Lobsang Tenchoe 10219 Views 0 Comments By Tsering Choephel DHARAMSALA, 10 Jan: Chinese authorities are conducting door-to-door inspections to enforce a ban on Tibetan children participating in private classes and engaging in religious activities during the winter break, as reported by Radio Free Asia on Tuesday, citing three sources within Tibet. According to the sources, the Chinese Education Department issued a notice earlier this month, reiterating the existing prohibition on Tibetan children participating in informal Tibetan language classes or workshops during their holidays. The notice instructs local authorities to intensify their supervision of Tibetans and take strict disciplinary action against those violating the rule. The report states that sources from Tibet’s capital, Lhasa, Labrang Monastery in Amdo province, and Kham Yushu have relayed information about local Chinese authorities in the area taking measures to ensure the strict enforcement of the notice issued by the Chinese Education Department. These measures include random checks in ‘residential areas and commercial establishments’ to investigate and prohibit informal language classes and workshops. The report also cites a notice issued by Lhasa city authorities on 30 November 2023. In the notice, parents are ordered to “ensure their children are completely free from the influence of religion” and to ensure they “voluntarily distance themselves from places of worship.” While the Education Department’s notice prohibits private and informal Tibetan language classes and other religious activities for Tibetan children, it allows them to attend classes and workshops taught by government-authorised individuals and organisations, with only subjects approved by the authorities allowed to be taught. “In the past, there was a strong tradition of providing supplementary, private tuitions to Tibetan children in the fields of Tibetan grammar, religion, math, and storytelling during their winter break,” said the report’s source from Amdo Labrang. “Now, only a few Chinese government-authorised organisations and individuals who carry out political re-education programs are allowed to give [lessons] to Tibetan students.” The intensifying control and and manipulation of education, at all levels across all sectors, occurs against the backdrop of China’s Patriotic Education Law passed in October 2023. This law, effective from the start of this year, aims to counter “historical nihilism” and safeguard “national unity,” covering ideology, politics, history, culture, national symbols, the beauty of the motherland, national unity, ethnic solidarity, national security and defence, and the deeds of heroes, as reported by Chinese state-run Xinhua. The law adheres to the principles enshrined in Xi Jinping’s Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics, Marxism-Leninism, Deng Xiaoping Thought, and Mao Zedong Thought. In the already suppressed regions of occupied Tibet, the CCP’s intensifying assimilative drive is becoming alarming and consequential. “With the prohibition of the study of Tibetan language, both in schools and in out-of-school programs, it has now become increasingly evident that young Tibetan children have lost touch with their native language and identity, a very alarming and concerning development,” the report quoted a source from Tibet as saying. China’s state-run boarding schools in Tibet, according to the Tibet Action Institutes’ 2021 report, estimate that over 1 million Tibetan children and adolescents between the ages of 4 to 18 are separated from their families and live in these schools, which rights groups describe as CCP’s “colonial-style boarding schools.” In February 2023, UN experts warned of the threat of CCP’s “mandatory large-scale programme intended to assimilate Tibetans into the majority Han culture” to the Tibetans’ distinct linguistic and cultural heritage. In August, US Secretary of State Antony Blinken, in a press conference, condemned the Beijings’ coercive policies that “seek to eliminate Tibet’s distinct linguistic, cultural, and religious traditions among younger generations of Tibetans,” and announced that it would impose visa restrictions on Chinese officials involved in CCP’s “forced assimilation” policy. The European Parliament in December adopted a resolution condemning “the repressive assimilation policies throughout China, especially the boarding school system in Tibet,” calling for immediate “abolishment of the system”

title: China’s Continuous Dam Project in Tibet: Threat to Neighbors and Environment
author: Lobsang Tenchoe
content: Front Slider News Tibet 25th January 2024 25th January 2024 Lobsang Tenchoe 8085 Views 0 Comments By Tsering Choephel DHARAMSALA 25 Jan: China’s construction of a new dam in Tibet’s Purang region in Ngari has reportedly been completed, indicating significant strategic implications for neighbouring countries such as India and Nepal, according to a Newsweek.com report on January 22. The observation is made from satellite imagery from Sinergise’s Sentinel Hub website, which renders photographs captured by the Sentinel-2 satellite of the European Union’s Copernicus earth observation program. The report notes that the dam’s construction began in July 2021. The dam is built on Mapcha Tsangpo (Peacock River), originating near Mount Kailash, a sacred site for devotees of Bon, Buddhists and Hindus. This perennial river, known as Ghaghara in India and the Karnali in Nepal, serves as a significant freshwater source for millions in western Nepal and the Northern plains of India. Built north of Purang in Tibet’s Ngari prefecture, the dam is approximately 18 miles north of Nepal’s border town of Hilsa and roughly 37 miles east of the Indian border. China’s extensive development of mega-dam projects on Tibet’s rivers has raised concerns among downstream riparian countries, affecting ecology, livelihoods, and triggering concerns of what experts called “hydro-hegemony.” In addition to the dam, China has constructed a new Ali Pulan Airport in the region. This dual-use facility, designed for both civilian and military purposes in border areas, officially became operational late last month, according to the report. Sana Hashmi, a postdoctoral fellow at the Taiwan-Asia Exchange Foundation think tank in Taipei, emphasised India’s natural concern about the potential long-term repercussions of Chinese activities saying “Understanding China’s hydro-behaviour with other neighbours is crucial in deciphering its hegemonic approach that has gone unchecked as of now”. Reportedly, Beijing halted sharing hydrological information with New Delhi in 2017, and the renewed data-sharing contract came at a cost of over $19 million for information from three hydrological stations, according to a 2022 investigation by The Quint news. China’s damming project at Tibet’s Yarlung Tsangpo is also a significant point of friction in India-China relations due to its strategic potential to control freshwater access to the downstream Brahmaputra. The Yarlung Tsangpo, in the east of their long and disputed border, is a critical source of fresh water for India’s northeastern regions and Bangladesh, as per the report. Mark Giordano and Anya Wahal, experts at Georgetown University’s Walsh School of Foreign Service argued that “The Brahmaputra would appear to be at the top of the list of conflict hotspots. The river is shared between four states, including the world’s two most populous, China and India. Both have rapidly growing economies, and both are already among the most water-stressed in the world.” In recent years, India has protested China’s construction of hydropower projects by refusing to purchase electricity from sites with Chinese investment, such as the Chameliya hydropower station in Nepal, built with Beijing’s financial aid. China is currently constructing another dam in the Purang region. According to the report, construction began in December 2022, as reported by China’s state-run media Xinhua . This project could extend China’s control over the Tibet river system upstream from the Mapcha Tsangpo, potentially leading to severe consequences downstream. Amidst these developments lies the fragile ecosystem of Tibet’s plateau, considered critically and globally significant in the context of accelerating climate change. Tibetans in exile, represented by the Central Tibetan Administration (CTA), environmental organizations, and others, have intensified and expanded Tibet’s environmental campaigns internationally. They align these efforts with the global climate change movement under the theme of ‘Tibet – the Third Pole’.

title: Tibetan leadership congratulates Taiwan’s president-elect Lai
author: Lobsang Tenchoe
content: Exile Front Slider News 16th January 2024 17th January 2024 Lobsang Tenchoe 7372 Views 0 Comments By Tsering Choephel DHARAMSALA, 16 Jan: His Holiness the Dalai Lama on Sunday offered his congratulations to Mr Lai Ching-te, the Taiwanese President-Elect for his victory and wished him “success in meeting the challenges that lie ahead.” Taiwan’s highly anticipated 2024 general election ended on Saturday with the Democratic Progressive Party’s (DPP) candidate Lai Ching-te winning the unprecedented third consecutive victory for the party. He is to replace the two-time president Tsai In-wen in May. The Dalai Lama in his missive noted that “observing the exercise of democracy, as has just taken place in Taiwan, is a source of encouragement for all of us who aspire to live in freedom and dignity.” Rated as one of the freest countries in the world by the 2023 Human Freedom Index and its robust practices of liberal democratic system considered exemplary, Taiwan however faces surmounting pressure and threats from the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) ruled China. China’s President Xi Jinping has declared multiple times that Taiwan’s unification with mainland China is inevitable, with the use of ‘force’ not ruled out to achieve the goal. Beijing claims Taiwan as a part of it while the democratically self-ruled island sees itself as distinct from mainland China. Surveys, as reported in several outlets, show that the vast majority of Taiwanese oppose CCP’s reunification threat and support the current status of de-facto independent Taiwan. The Dalai Lama, as a strong believer and proponent of peace and dialogue for world peace said “Good relations between Taiwan and the People’s Republic of China are of utmost importance. It is my longstanding conviction that engaging in dialogue is the best way to resolve difficult issues, whether on a local, national or international level.” In a post on X, formerly Twitter, Sikyong (President) Penpa Tsering, the political head of the exiled Tibetans extended his congratulations to Lai. “As a democracy in exile, Tibetans profoundly admire the spirit of self-determination exemplified by the people of Taiwan.” Deputy Speaker of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile (TPiE), Dolma Tsering Teykhang also congratulated the President-elect Lai. Declaring CTA and the TPiE as legitimate representatives and the voices of Tibet, she said “We have worked closely with the Taiwan Democratic Foundation to learn from each other on our shared interest and we hope to further strengthen our ties through enhancing people-to-people connections in future.” The world leaders, including US Secretary of State Antony Blinken, Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos, UK’s foreign secretary David Cameroon and others welcomed the victory of Taiwanese president-elect William Lai, who Beijing has labelled as a ‘dangerous separatist’. As usual, Beijing hit back, calling it “gross interference in China’s internal affairs.” To Beijing’s delight, Naura – a tiny island country reportedly announced on Monday that it was severing ties with Taiwan and establishing them with Beijing. That leaves Taiwan with just 12 nations around the world that formally recognise it. Yet, the significance of Taiwan as a democratic sovereign country has gained momentum in recent years, with escalating threats from authoritarian China and mounting support from the US-led free world.

title: Rescheduled Visit: Dalai Lama to visit Sikkim in December
author: Lobsang Tenchoe
content: Exile Front Slider News 28th November 2023 28th November 2023 Lobsang Tenchoe 8613 Views 0 Comments By Tsering Choephel A file photo of His Holiness the Dalai Lama. DHARAMSALA, 28 Nov: His Holiness the Dalai Lama, the spiritual head of Tibet is confirmed to visit Gangtok, Sikkim, on 11 December 2023, according to the circular issued by the Government of Sikkim’s Home Department and as per the Dalai Lama’s schedule announced on his official website. During his visit, on 12 December, the Dalai Lama will give a one-day teaching on Gyalsey Thokme Sangpo’s ’ 37 Practices of a Bodhisattva’ (laklen sodunma) in the morning at Paljor Stadium, which has a capacity of 30,000 people. The Dalai Lama is also scheduled to give a general teaching followed by the ‘Ceremony for Generation of Bodhicitta’ at Sed-Gyued Monastery in Salugara, West Bengal, on 14 December. His visit to Gangtok, the capital of Sikkim state in northeast India, initially planned from 16 to 22 October, was postponed due to the flash floods caused by a cloudburst at Teesta River. The visit, later scheduled in the month of November, was cancelled at the advice of his personal physicians for the Dalai Lama’s full recovery from his bout of flu. The Dalai Lama had bestowed the 17th and 24th Kalachakra Teachings in Gangtok in 1993 and Salugara in 1996, respectively. Following his visit and teachings in Sikkim and West Bengal, the Tibetan Nobel laureate will be visiting Bodhgaya, Bihar, with a series of programs and teachings scheduled in the month of December until the 1st of January, on which a long life prayer will be offered to him in the morning at the Kalachakra Teaching Ground, as per his schedule listed on his official website.

title: 5th Annual General Meeting of Europe Tibetan Communities Concludes Successfully in Berlin
author: oot_admin
content: The 5th Annual General Meeting of Tibetan Communities in Europe was successfully held on from 29-30 August 2026 bringing all key stakeholders from across Europe to deliberate on Tibetan identity, culture and language preservation, efforts to advancing the Tibet’s unresolved conflict on the international platform. The conference commenced with a special video message from Sikyong Penpa Tsering of the Central Tibetan Administration. In his message, Sikyong underscored the importance of unity, collective responsibility, and active community engagement in addressing the challenges facing Tibetans worldwide and stressed importance of understanding the content of so called “Promotion of Ethnic Unity and Progress law” of China and risk poses by it. He also expressed his appreciation to the organisers and participants for their continued dedication to strengthening Tibetan communities across Europe and advancing the Tibetan cause. In the Meeting distinguished participants included Members of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile, Thupten Gyatso and Tenzin Yangkar; Thinlay Chukki, Representative of the Office of Tibet, Geneva; Tsering Yangkey, Representative of the Office of Tibet, London; Rigzin Choedon Genkhang, Representative of the Office of Tibet, Brussels; Tenchoe Gyatso, President of the International Campaign for Tibet (ICT); Thupten Tsering, Office of Tibet, Paris; and Dhundup Gyalpo, Tibetan Liaison Officer for Europe. The conference was also attended by the presidents, vice presidents, and executive committee members of 11 Tibetan communities across Europe, reflecting a strong commitment to collective action and cooperation among Tibetan communities on the continent. Delegates also exchanged experiences, shared best practices, and explored new approaches to addressing the evolving needs and aspirations of the Tibetan diaspora. The conference reaffirmed the importance of solidarity, collaboration, and shared responsibility in safeguarding Tibetan identity and advancing the collective interests of Tibetan communities in Europe. Participants emphasised the empowering the younger generations, and enhance coordinated advocacy efforts in support of Tibet and the Tibetan people. Following two days of extensive deliberations, the conference concluded with the adoption of a four-point resolution and Berlin Declaration. (1) Renewed efforts to preserve and promote Tibetan identity, language, and cultural heritage among younger generations; Condemn those who defames His Holiness the great 14th Dalai Lama or frame baseless allegation against His Holiness; (2) Promote unifying efforts to carry out all activities and initiatives for Tibet and Tibetan with new slogan “I am Tibetan”and “We are Tibetan”; (3) Strengthen an Advocacy and lobbying initiatives to raise international awareness of the critical situation inside Tibet and support the just cause of the Tibetan people; and expand coordinated campaigns and outreach activities across Europe to garner greater public and political support for Tibet. (4) Confirmation of next general meeting in year 2028 will be held in Paris for 3 days and formation of new drafting committee to draft Europe Tibetan Communities Meetings guideline and regulations. The meeting attracted 27 participants, reflecting strong youth involvement, with a considerable number of attendees in their early twenties. The 5th Europe Tibetan Communities Meeting was organised by the Tibetan Association Germany and Office of Tibet, Geneva.

title: Representative Thinlay Chukki and UN Advocacy Officer Phuntsok Topgyal Conclude Intensive Geneva Advocacy, Urge Global Action on Tibet Ahead of UNHRC Session
author: oot_admin
content: Thinlay Chukki, Representative of His Holiness the Dalai Lama, and Phuntsok Topgyal, UN Advocacy Officer at the Office of Tibet, Geneva, have concluded an intensive week of diplomatic advocacy in Geneva ahead of the 63rd Session of the United Nations Human Rights Council, taking place from 7 September to 9 October 2026. From 17 to 24 August, the Tibetan representatives engaged with representatives of more than 32 countries, including EU Member States, other Permanent Missions, OHCHR officials and UN Special Procedures mandate holders. The advocacy sought to ensure that the deteriorating human rights situation in Tibet remains firmly on the international agenda. A central concern raised was the self-immolation of Lobga Rangzen, who died after setting himself on fire outside the United Nations Headquarters in New York on 2 July 2026, reportedly while carrying a Tibetan flag and protesting China’s policies toward Tibet. The delegation stressed that his death should not be viewed as an isolated tragedy, but understood within the broader context of policies that Tibetans say are undermining their identity, language, culture, religion and fundamental freedoms. Particular attention was drawn to the implementation of China’s Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress, and concerns over its potential implications for Tibetans and other ethnic communities. The delegation emphasised that laws presented as promoting ethnic unity must not become instruments of forced assimilation or the erosion of distinct linguistic, cultural and religious identities. The delegation also raised concerns regarding religious freedom and the future reincarnation and succession of His Holiness the Dalai Lama, stressing that Tibetan religious affairs must be determined by Tibetans themselves, without interference from the Chinese government. Other issues included developments at Larung Gar Buddhist Academy and other Tibetan religious institutions, as well as the rapid expansion of hydropower dams and infrastructure across the Tibetan Plateau, with potential environmental, social, cultural and human-rights consequences. A particularly strong concern was the absence of a meaningful public response from the United Nations to Lobga Rangzen’s self-immolation outside its headquarters. The delegation questioned how such a profound act of protest could take place at the doorstep of the world’s foremost international organisation without receiving substantive attention within the UN human rights system. It urged Member States, OHCHR and relevant Special Procedures mandate holders to examine the circumstances surrounding his death and the wider human rights conditions underlying his protest. The delegation welcomed the serious engagement shown by many of the representatives and officials it met and expressed hope that the concerns raised will lead to concrete diplomatic action during the 63rd Human Rights Council session, including public statements, interventions, questions to China and engagement with relevant UN human rights mechanisms. The forthcoming Council session must not become another occasion where Tibet is discussed only behind closed doors while remaining absent from the public record. As policies described by Tibetan representatives as mechanisms of assimilation continue to expand, the international community has a responsibility to ensure that Tibet does not become a forgotten human rights crisis.

title: Tibetans in Switzerland Hold Peaceful Protest Outside UN Office in Geneva to Mark 49th Day Since Martyrdom of Lobga Rangzen
author: oot_admin
content: On 22 August 2026, Tibetans in Switzerland gathered in front of the United Nations Office at the historic Palais des Nations in Geneva to mark the 49th day following the self-immolation of Tibetan martyr Lobga Rangzen and to hold a peaceful demonstration calling international attention to China’s continued repression in Tibet, particularly through the enactment of the “Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress.” The protesters first assembled in front of Palais Wilson, the headquarters of the UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR), before peacefully marching towards the Palais des Nations. They carried placards and chanted slogans condemning the PRC’s new assimilative legislation. Representative Thinlay Chukki of the Office of Tibet (Geneva), the Abbot of Rikon Monastery, His Holiness the Dalai Lama’s former Special Envoy Kelsang Gyaltsen, former Representative Kelsang Dorjee, and members of Tibetan communities from across the Swiss Confederation participated in the protest. As the march concluded at the United Nations Office, Representative Thinlay Chukki addressed the gathering, emphasising the need for Tibetans to also chant slogans in English, French, and German to raise awareness among the wider community in the region. She further highlighted the importance of carrying forward the final messages of Tibetan martyr Lobga Rangzen and expressed her appreciation to everyone who participated in the demonstration.

title: UN Advocacy Officer Phuntsok Topgyal Attends Tibet Festival 2026 Celebrating Tibetan Culture in Basel
author: oot_admin
content: The Regional Tibetan Community of Basel, in collaboration with the Gesellschaft Schweizerisch-Tibetische Freundschaft (GSTF), organised its annual Tibet Festival in Basel from 21 to 23 August 2026. The three-day festival brought together members of the Tibetan community, Swiss friends, local residents and distinguished guests to celebrate and promote Tibetan culture and heritage. Among those attending were Hon. Maya Graf, Member of the Council of States representing the Canton of Basel-Landschaft; Gianna Hablützel-Bürki, Member of the Grand Council of the Canton of Basel-Stadt; Phuntsok Topgyal, the UN Advocacy Officer at the Office of Tibet Geneva; Thomas, President of GSTF; and other invited guests. The festival featured a vibrant programme of Tibetan and Swiss music, traditional Tibetan dances, Yak and Lion dances, handicraft displays and traditional Tibetan cuisine. Visitors also had the opportunity to learn about Tibetan history, cultural traditions and heritage through exhibitions and interactions with members of the Tibetan community. During the festival, Phuntsok Topgyal expressed his appreciation to the distinguished guests and visitors for their participation and for helping to highlight and promote Tibetan culture and heritage. He also briefed attendees on the current situation in Tibet, including the recent case of Lobga Rangzen, and shared information about the challenges facing Tibetans under the current policies in Tibet. He further introduced the structure and functions of the Central Tibetan Administration (CTA) and explained its objectives and efforts to represent the Tibetan people and preserve Tibet’s unique cultural, linguistic and religious heritage. The interaction provided an opportunity for Swiss guests and members of the wider public to gain a better understanding of both Tibetan culture and the current situation in Tibet. A special feature of this year’s festival was an exhibition on Thokchak, presented by Christine, the owner of a museum in Basel, offering visitors an opportunity to learn about its cultural and historical significance. The festival served as an important platform for cultural exchange and mutual understanding between the Tibetan and Swiss communities. The organisers expressed their appreciation to all guests, performers, volunteers and visitors for their participation and support in making the Tibet Festival 2026 a successful celebration of Tibetan culture and heritage.

title: Tibetan Community of Austria Commemorates 49th Day of Prayer for Lobga Rangzen
author: oot_admin
content: The Tibetan Community of Austria observed the 49th day since the passing of Pawo Lobga Rangzen with solemn prayer ceremonies in Vienna, Linz and Salzburg on 20 August, 2026. In Vienna, the main prayer gathering was held at the Panchen Losang Chogyen Gelug Centre, where community members offered prayers and dedicated merits for the peaceful rebirth of Lobga Rangzen and for all Tibetans who have sacrificed their lives for the Tibetan cause. Similar prayer gatherings in Linz and Salzburg reflected the solidarity and unity of Tibetans across Austria. The commemorations also served as a peaceful reminder of the continuing human rights situation in Tibet and the importance of preserving Tibetan identity, culture, language and religion. The Tibetan Community of Austria expressed its profound respect for Lobga Rangzen and reaffirmed its commitment to peaceful advocacy for the rights and dignity of the Tibetan people.

title: Tibetan Communities Across Europe Commemorate 49th Day of Lobga Rangzen’s Self-Immolation in Geneva
author: oot_admin
content: More than 1,000 Tibetans and supporters from across Europe gathered in Geneva on Wednesday, 19 August, to commemorate the 49th day since the self-immolation of Lobga Rangzen in front of the United Nations Headquarters in New York and to call on the international community to uphold the rights, identity and freedom of the Tibetan people. The large-scale demonstration and prayer gathering began with a march from Palais Wilson to the United Nations Office at Geneva, culminating near the Broken Chair, a longstanding symbol of opposition to landmines and violence. In the evening, participants gathered at the same location for a candlelight prayer ceremony in remembrance of Lobga Rangzen and his sacrifice. The commemoration brought together Tibetan communities and organisations from Switzerland and Liechtenstein, Germany, the Netherlands, Spain, France, Austria, Sweden, Italy and the United Kingdom, alongside the Swiss Tibetan Women’s Association, the Gesellschaft Schweizerisch-Tibetische Freundschaft (GSTF), the Tibetan Youth Association in Europe (TYAE), and V-TAG. Tibetan community leaders from across Europe also addressed the gathering. Among the distinguished guests present were Cédric Jeanneret, Member of the Grand Council of Geneva, who attended and addressed the gathering, and Merce, Secretary of UNPO, who also delivered remarks. Thomas Buchli, President of GSTF, read a Statement from the Swiss Parliamentary Group for Tibet. Representatives of the French-speaking Swiss Tibetan Friends group also spoke in solidarity with the Tibetan cause. Representing the Tibet Bureau Geneva, Representative Thinlay Chukki, together with Phuntsok Topgyal, UN Advocacy Officer, and Sangye Kep, EU-China Liaison Officer, attended the demonstration. Representative Thinlay Chukki addressed the gathering and stressed that the commemoration was not only an expression of remembrance, but also a renewed appeal to the international community to act. In her remarks, Representative Thinlay Chukki said that the gathering in front of the United Nations was particularly significant because it marked the 49th day since Lobga Rangzen sacrificed his life in front of the UN Headquarters in New York. “As we assemble today here, we want to commemorate his sacrifice, but also signal to the international community that we have not lost faith and hope yet.” She recalled that Tibetans in exile, under the leadership of His Holiness the Dalai Lama, have consistently spoken for the rights and freedom of Tibetans inside Tibet since 1959. She said Lobga Rangzen’s sacrifice reflected the profound distress caused by policies that, in the Tibetan community’s view, threaten Tibet’s cultural identity, language and heritage. Representative Chukki strongly criticised the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law, saying that its implementation represents a serious threat to Tibetan identity and cultural rights. She expressed concern that the law could further restrict the preservation and use of the Tibetan language and culture and intensify restrictions on those advocating for Tibetan rights. She further warned that provisions targeting organisations and individuals who support Tibetan rights could contribute to transnational repression, extending the impact of restrictive policies beyond Tibet’s borders. “Therefore, I want to say to the United Nations, to the international community and the international organisations, we are here today to not only show a protest against the Chinese law, but also to state that we still have hope that you will stand for Tibetans, for Tibet and for Tibetans inside Tibet,” she said. Addressing the UN human rights mechanisms and governments directly, Representative Chukki urged the UN Special Procedures, the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, ambassadors and governments to move beyond expressions of concern and take meaningful action. “It is no longer okay to be silent. It is time that you stand up and speak and act on the words that you have committed for.” She also called on Tibetans and their supporters not to lose hope, emphasising the importance of unity and sustained international solidarity. The commemoration concluded with prayers and a candlelight ceremony near the Broken Chair. Participants observed the 49th day in remembrance of Lobga Rangzen, while reaffirming their commitment to peaceful advocacy for Tibet and calling on the international community to stand with Tibetans facing restrictions on their language, culture, religion and identity. A symbolic hair-cutting ceremony was also held during the commemoration, adding a deeply emotional and cultural dimension to the day’s events. The gathering served as a powerful demonstration of solidarity among Tibetans across Europe and their international supporters. Standing before the United Nations, participants renewed their appeal for the UN and governments to uphold universal human rights and to ensure that the voices and rights of Tibetans inside Tibet are neither ignored nor forgotten. The message from Geneva was clear: Lobga Rangzen’s sacrifice must not be forgotten, and the international community must not remain silent in the face of policies that threaten the survival of Tibet’s distinct identity, language and cultural heritage.

title: Over 200 Tibetans and Supporters Gather in Bern to Protest China’s Intensifying Assimilation Policies and Honour Lobga Rangzen
author: oot_admin
content: More than 200 Tibetans and supporters gathered near the Swiss Parliament in Bern on Friday, 14 August, for a peaceful demonstration protesting China’s intensifying assimilation policies in Tibet. The gathering also marked the 44th day since the self-immolation of Tibetan activist Lobga Rangzen, whose death has renewed international attention to the human rights situation inside Tibet. The demonstration was jointly organised by the Tibetan Community in Switzerland and Liechtenstein, the Swiss Tibetan Friendship Association (GSTF), the Swiss Tibetan Women’s Association, the European Tibetan Youth Association, and Swiss V-TAG. Among those attending were Tibetan community leaders, former Tibetan parliamentarians, former representatives of the Tibet Bureau, and representatives of the Tibet Bureau in Geneva, including Thinlay Chukki, Representative of His Holiness the Dalai Lama, and Phuntsok Topgyal, UN Advocacy Officer. The gathering featured a series of solidarity activities, including the chanting of slogans, a scarf-presentation ceremony in front of a portrait of Pawo Lobga Rangzen, the singing of the Tibetan national anthem, a one-minute silence in memory of Tibetan martyrs, and prayers for peace. Representatives of each organising organisation addressed the gathering, highlighting the ongoing human rights concerns in Tibet and honouring the sacrifice of Lobga Rangzen. They called on Switzerland, the United Nations, and the international community to take stronger and more concrete action in response to the deteriorating human rights situation in Tibet. Representative Thinlay Chukki expressed her gratitude to the Tibetan community and supporters who had gathered in Bern to honour the memory of Lobga Rangzen and raise international awareness of the continuing human rights violations in Tibet. “Today, as we commemorate the 44th day since the self-immolation of Lobga Rangzen, I would like to sincerely thank all my fellow Tibetans who have gathered here in Bern, not only to remember his sacrifice, but also to remind the international community of the atrocities that Tibetans in Tibet continue to face,” she said. Chukki also thanked representatives of the Swiss Tibetan Friendship Association, the Tibetan Women’s Association, the Tibetan Youth Association, and other non-governmental organisations for their participation in the demonstration. Referring to Lobga Rangzen’s self-immolation, Chukki said his sacrifice should serve as a powerful call for the international community to pay greater attention to the human rights situation inside Tibet. “Since 2009, we have seen 157 known cases of self-immolation inside Tibet, and each of these self-immolators has called for freedom in Tibet and the return of His Holiness the Dalai Lama,” she said. On behalf of His Holiness the Dalai Lama and the Central Tibetan Administration, she expressed profound gratitude to those who had sacrificed their lives and offered reassurance to their families that Tibetans in exile would continue working towards the restoration of freedom in Tibet. A major focus of Chukki’s address was China’s Ethnic Unity and Progress Law, adopted on 12 March 2026 and brought into force on 1 July 2026. She strongly criticised the legislation, arguing that it further institutionalises policies that threaten Tibet’s distinct cultural, linguistic, religious, and national identity. “It is unfathomable that the Chinese government has the audacity not only to egregiously violate Tibetans’ fundamental freedoms and human rights, but also to legalise such assimilation through legislation,” she stated. Chukki warned that the policies went beyond cultural assimilation and described the situation in Tibet as cultural genocide. She highlighted provisions relating to the prioritisation of Mandarin Chinese, increased state control over Tibetan monasteries, and measures that, she said, could also affect people outside China who support the Tibetan cause. “This law not only impacts Tibetans inside Tibet, but also every supporter who has stood with us and supported our struggle for freedom in Tibet,” she said. She called on the international community to take urgent and concrete action to ensure that the human rights of Tibetans are respected and protected in accordance with international law. Chukki also urged the United Nations to take concrete steps to investigate the human rights situation in Tibet. “The United Nations [must] take it upon itself to ensure that it sends a delegation to China, to Tibet, to document and record the human rights violations on the ground,” she said. She further appealed to the Swiss Government to increase diplomatic pressure on China to comply with international law and the treaties to which it is a party. On behalf of the Tibetan community, Chukki expressed appreciation to Switzerland’s Federal Department of Foreign Affairs for acknowledging Tibetan appeals and responding with serious concern regarding the situation in Tibet. She also thanked members of the Swiss Parliamentary Group for Tibet for their continued support and urged Swiss parliamentarians to consider appropriate resolutions to ensure that the human rights situation in Tibet remains firmly on Switzerland’s political agenda.

title: Representative Thinlay Chukki Sees Off the 105th Gaden Tripa on His Return to India
author: oot_admin
content: The 105th Gaden Tripa, Kyabje Jetsun Lobsang Dorje Palzangpo, concluded his religious engagements in Switzerland and departed for India on 5 August 2026. Before his departure, he was warmly seen off by the staff of theTibet Bureau, Geneva,led by Representative Thinlay Chukki, together with members of the local Tibetan community.

title: 13 Tibetan Associations Unite in Zurich in a Powerful Candlelight March to Honour Pawo Lobga Rangzen on the 33rd Day Since His Passing
author: oot_admin
content: Thirteen Tibetan associations in Switzerland jointly organised a peaceful candle march in Zurich on 5 August 2026 to commemorate the 33rd day since the passing of Tibetan self-immolator Pawo Lobga Rangzen. More than 700 people participated in the march, which began at Werdmühleplatz Zurich and proceeded towards the Chinese Embassy in Zurich. During the programme, representatives of the organising associations delivered speeches and jointly read a press statement explaining the purpose of the gathering and remembering Lobga Rangzen’s final message. The Tibet Bureau Geneva’s UN Advocacy Officer, Phuntsok Topgyal, attended the event on behalf of Representative Thinlay Chukki. In his address, he spoke about the circumstances surrounding Lobga Rangzen’s self-immolation, including the location, timing, final message, and the circumstances of his passing. Phuntsok Topgyal stated that Lobga Rangzen carried out his self-immolation following the implementation of what he described as China’s ethnic unity and related policies, which, according to him, threatened Tibetan culture, language, and identity. He said that Lobga Rangzen’s action was intended to draw international attention to the situation in Tibet, seek greater international support for the Tibetan cause, and call for the repeal of those policies. Speaking about Lobga Rangzen’s final message, Phuntsok Topgyal emphasised that his words should not be interpreted as suggesting that Tibetans lack unity. Phuntsok Topgyal said,“Today, more than 700 people have gathered for this protest, and 13 different Tibetan associations have come together to organise this event. This reflects the unity of our people.” He further explained that Lobga Rangzen had witnessed the situation inside Tibet, experienced life in exile in India, and observed the decades of dedicated work carried out by His Holiness the Dalai Lama for Tibet and the Tibetan people. After moving to the United States, Lobga Rangzen also witnessed the lives of Tibetans living in the diaspora. According to Phuntsok Topgyal, Lobga Rangzen acknowledged that many Tibetans overseas had achieved economic stability and had himself said,“It is not that I lack food or shelter. I have everything.”However, despite having a comfortable life, he carried deep emotional pain every day because, in his view, some Tibetans who fully understood the situation in Tibet had nevertheless become involved with the Chinese government. Phuntsok Topgyal said that this was why Lobga Rangzen urged Tibetans to remember their identity, encouraging everyone to think,“I am Tibetan.” Phuntsok Topgyal also explained why Lobga Rangzen chose the United Nations Headquarters in New York, rather than the Chinese Embassy, as the location for his self-immolation. He noted that Lobga Rangzen was not the first person to self-immolate in front of the UN Headquarters in New York. According to him, Roger Allen LaPorte self-immolated there in 1965 in protest against the Vietnam War, making Lobga Rangzen the second known person to do so. He also noted that there have been three recorded incidents of self-immolation in front of the United Nations Office at Geneva. According to Phuntsok Topgyal, while Lobga Rangzen was not the first Tibetan to self-immolate, he was the first Tibetan to carry out a self-immolation in front of the United Nations Headquarters in New York. Recalling Lobga Rangzen’s final moments, Phuntsok Topgyal said that, despite suffering extreme pain, he remained calm and did not run, shout, or jump. Instead, he stood motionless, “like a burning lamp or candle.” According to Phuntsok Topgyal, after his body had been severely burned, Lobga Rangzen slowly lowered himself, extended his hands forward, and fell into a full prostration facing the United Nations Headquarters building. Phuntsok Topgyal said this reflected Lobga Rangzen’s belief that, even in his final moments, the United Nations Headquarters was akin to a temple, a place where his prayers and message could reach the international community and where support for the Tibetan cause might be found. Phuntsok Topgyal further stated that Lobga Rangzen’s decision reflected his commitment to the principles of non-violence taught by His Holiness the Dalai Lama. He said that although Lobga Rangzen could have chosen violence, he instead followed the path of non-violence and sacrificed his life to convey his message to Tibetans and to the wider international community. In his closing remarks, Phuntsok Topgyal expressed concern that more than one month had passed since Lobga Rangzen’s self-immolation, yet, according to him, the United Nations had not publicly responded. He called on Tibetans around the world to continue submitting appeals and messages of concern to the United Nations, parliamentarians, and governments in order to promote greater international awareness and support for the Tibetan cause. He added that while international recognition alone may not restore Tibet’s freedom, acknowledging Lobga Rangzen’s sacrifice would ensure that his action is recorded in international history as a peaceful self-immolation carried out in front of the United Nations Headquarters in New York for the cause of Tibetan freedom. He concluded by expressing the hope that representatives of all 193 United Nations Member States would have the opportunity to learn about and better understand the Tibetan issue and the message left behind by Pawo Lobga Rangzen.

title: Austria Tibetan Community Leads Peaceful Rally to Mark One Month Since Pawo Lobga Rangzen’s Passing
author: oot_admin
content: Tibetan communities and supporters around the world are organising a global day of action to commemorate Pawo Lobga Rangzen, who carried out a self-immolation on 2 July 2026, in front of the United Nations Headquarters in New York, United States. The action has drawn attention from Tibetan communities, human rights advocates, and supporters worldwide, who are using this occasion to raise awareness about the ongoing concerns surrounding human rights, cultural preservation, and the future of the Tibetan people. On 2 August 2026 marks one month since the passing of Pawo Lobga Rangzen. In remembrance, Tibetan communities and solidarity groups in different parts of the world are organising peaceful gatherings, demonstrations, and awareness activities. In Vienna, Austria, a joint peaceful protest rally is being organised by the Tibetan Community, Voluntary Tibet Advocacy Group (VTAG), Save Tibet, Students for a Free Tibet (SFT), and Friends of Tibet. The rally will begin in front of the Chinese Embassy and proceed towards Stephansplatz. Participants are expected to gather to express their solidarity and to call for greater international attention to the human rights situation in Tibet. The organisers stated that the demonstration aims to provide a platform for Tibetans and supporters to peacefully express their concerns, remember the sacrifice of Pawo Lobga Rangzen, and highlight issues related to human rights, religious freedom, cultural identity, and the preservation of Tibetan heritage. The event is also intended to encourage governments, international organisations, and the global community to continue monitoring developments related to Tibet and to support peaceful dialogue and respect for fundamental human rights. Tibetan communities and supporters participating in the worldwide activities have emphasised that the gatherings will be conducted peacefully and with respect for public order, while seeking to amplify awareness and international engagement on issues affecting Tibetans.

title: アリヤ・ツェワン・ギャルポ代表、東京の人文学フォーラムで在日中国人らと対話
author: Tashi Yangzom
content: 東京：中国系の学術シンクタンクである「東京人文学論壇（Tokyo Humanities Forum）」は、「世界平和のための中国とチベット」をテーマにした講演および討論会を開催し、8月16日に東京都新宿区（早稲田町）の会場へ、ダライ・ラマ法王日本・東アジア代表部事務所の代表であるアリヤ・ツェワン・ギャルポ博士を招き、講演を行った。 フォーラムの幹事長であり、亡命中の中国の人権派弁護士である李金星（リー・ジンシン）氏が、日中の参加者およびメディア関係者を歓迎した。同氏はアリヤ代表を聴衆に紹介し、中国チベット問題およびその解決の必要性について簡潔に説明した。 アリヤ代表は、中国コミュニティと直接対話する機会を提供してくれた主催者に謝意を述べた。この対話が、中国共産党（CCP）体制が両コミュニティの間に作り出してきた多くの疑念や誤解を解く助けとなるからだ。 代表は、亡命中のチベット人、中国人、ウイグル人、南モンゴル人、香港人が、自由、民主主義、正義の追求において皆同じ立場にあり、この目的の一体性こそが、母国における弾圧や不正義と闘うために団結の力となるべきであると語った。また、チベット人は、天安門広場の中国人学生の要求や闘争、ノーベル平和賞受賞者である劉暁波氏らによる「08憲章」の請願、2020年の香港デモ参加者の要求、そして2022年の「白紙革命」を通じた中国の人々の要求に連帯を感じていると述べた。 さらに、中国の人々とチベットの人々の要求は同じであり、それらの要求は中国憲法の枠内のものであるにもかかわらず、中国共産党政権が国家憲法を踏みにじっていると詳説した。そして、ダライ・ラマ法王とチベット亡命政府が掲げる「中道アプローチ」は、中国チベット問題の解決だけでなく、中国とチベットが世界平和と安定の推進においてより大きな役割を果たすことを可能にするものであると語った。 40名を超える日中の学者や知識人が討論に参加し、チベットの自治の性質、ダライ・ラマ法王の転生とその後の影響、中国の民族団結法とその進展、焼身抗議などについて質問を投げかけた。中国の民主化後にチベット人は独立を主張しないのかという質問に対し、アリヤ代表は、「まず畑を手に入れずして、収穫の取り分を議論するのは時期尚早であり、本質的ではない」と回答した。 中国人の参加者からは、今回のイベントを通じてチベット人の視点や願いがより明確に理解できたこと、またチベット人は中国共産党政権が描くような反中・反中国人ではないことが分かったとして、主催者に対し同様のイベントの継続を求める声があがった。 会場では、アリヤ・ツェワン・ギャルポ代表の著作の『チベットの反論』の中国語版や、中道アプローチに関する書籍、植民地的寄宿制学校に関する報告書が参加者に配布された。また、台湾のチベット事務所は、ダライ・ラマ法王の著作『声なきものの声』の中国語版を数冊、イベントに際して寄贈した。 通訳は浦氏が務め、チベットハウス・ジャパンのチサ・ツェラ氏が司会進行および参加者への書籍配布の調整を補佐した。当日の討論の様子はこちら。 ――ダライ・ラマ法王日本代表部事務所による報告

title: 故ロブガ・ランゼン氏 四十九日法要のご案内
author: Tashi Yangzom
content: Unite for TIBET – Global Day of Action 映画「ルンタ」上映＆監督トーク 21 Jul at 10:02 am

title: チベット通信 2026年 夏号 SUMMER ISSUE

title: Unite for TIBET – Global Day of Action 　 映画「ルンタ」上映＆監督トーク
author: Tashi Yangzom
content: 中国の「民族団結進歩促進法」に抗い、2026年7月2日、在米チベット人ロブカ・ランゼンさんが国連本部前で焼身した。究極の非暴力の抵抗手段である焼身抗議はなぜ生まれてしまったのか？その背景に迫るドキュメンタリー映画「ルンタ」（2015制作/111分）。後半、カメラはチベット本土に潜入し、焼身抗議が起きた場所を巡りながら、いま世界が最も必要とする、チベット人の〈慈悲の心〉〈利他の心〉を描く。上映後、池谷薫監督を迎えトークがあります。

title: ダライ・ラマ法王の歩み　世界への祈り その生涯をたどる
author: Tashi Yangzom
content: ダライ・ラマ法王猊下90歳の御生誕を記念し、中央チベット政権は2025年7月から2026年7月までの1年間を「慈悲の年」と定めました。この記念の年にあたり、世界各国で祝賀行事が行われています。その一環として、日本では、ダライ・ラマ法王の御生涯と御使命を紹介する写真展を開催いたします。皆様のご来場を心よりお待ち申し上げております。

title: ネパール・チベット国境地帯における大規模土石流災害被災者への緊急支援のお願い Nepal-Tibet Flood Relief Fund
author: Tashi Yangzom
content: ネパール・チベット国境地帯における大規模土石流災害被災者への緊急支援のお願い このたび、ネパール・チベット国境地帯で発生した大規模な土石流災害により、お亡くなりになられた方々に謹んで哀悼の意を表しますとともに、被災された皆様に心よりお見舞い申し上げます。 この災害により、チベット側のキロン（吉隆）およびネパール側のラスワ郡において、川沿いに多数の家屋が押し流されるなど甚大な被害が発生しました。 ネパール政府が確認した今回の洪水による被害が特に深刻な地域には、5つのチベット人居住区もあります。 今回の災害により、被災地では多くの方々が住居や生活基盤を失い、現在も安否が確認されていない方々がいます。現地では、被災された方々の救命・救援活動とともに、食料、生活物資、住居など、緊急かつ継続的な支援が必要とされています。 チベットハウス・ジャパンは、今回の災害によって被災された方々への緊急救援・支援活動を支援するため、皆様からのご寄付をお願い申し上げます。 一人でも多くの被災者の方々の命が救われ、一日も早く安全で平穏な生活を取り戻すことができますよう、皆様の温かいご支援とご協力を心よりお願い申し上げます。 【ご寄付は下記口座へお振込みいただけます】※ご寄付受付は10月31日までとなります。 ■金融機関名：三菱UFJ銀行■支店名：新宿通支店（050）■口座種別：普通■口座番号：0001674■口座名義：特定非営利活動法人チベットハウスジャパン募金活動 ※領収書をご希望の方は、お名前・ご住所・電話番号・メールアドレスをお知らせください。 チベットハウス・ジャパン電話：03-5988-3576 /Eメール：[email protected]

title: アリヤ・ツェワン・ギャルポ代表、1週間のフィリピン訪問を終了
author: Tashi Yangzom
content: マニラ：ダライ・ラマ法王日本・東アジア代表部事務所のアリヤ・ツェワン・ギャルポ代表は、フィリピン公式訪問を終えた。一週間に及ぶ滞在中、ダライ・ラマ法王の生涯と使命に関する写真展と一連の講演会、ファー・イースタン大学およびフィリピン大学アジアセンターでのチベットについての講演、フィリピン国会議員らとの面会、マニラ市内での異宗教間対話への参加など精力的な活動を展開した。 チベットハウス・ジャパンは、ラモン・マグサイサイ賞財団（RMAF）との共催で、8月22日から25日まで同財団ホールにてダライ・ラマ法王の生涯と使命に関する4日間の写真展と講演会を開催した。財団の特別賓客をはじめ、学者、芸術家、学生、一般市民など多くの人々が会場を訪れ、講演を聞き、質疑応答に参加した。RMAFのスザンナ・B・アファン会長は開会の辞で聴衆を歓迎し、同財団とチベットの長年の関係、2003年および2004年のダライ・ラマ法王への謁見や平和と非暴力のメッセージについて語った。 アリヤ・ツェワン・ギャルポ代表は、写真展や講演会の開催にあたり温かいサポートをしてくれた財団へ謝意を表明した。また、1959年に同財団からダライ・ラマ法王に対するリーダーシップ賞の授与が、当時チベットで起きていたことへの関心を高めるうえで大いに役立ったことにも感謝の意を表した。さらに、1960年代初頭に国連でチベット問題が取り上げられた際におけるフィリピン政府と国民の支援にも謝辞を述べた。代表は来賓や学者、一般市民に対し、チベット問題を説明するとともに、ダライ・ラマ法王の4つの使命（人間の価値の促進、宗教間の調和の促進、チベット文化の保存、古代インドのナランダ仏教教学の復興）について詳しく述べ、これらすべての使命が、普遍的な責任感を伴う国際社会の実現に向けられていることを解説した。 写真展および講演会の開会式では、市内のニンマ派およびカギュ派のチベット人僧侶らが祈りの読誦を行った。 財団は書籍『He Will Be Called Great: The Life of H.H. the 14th Dalai Lama』を発行した。同書は著名な女優兼演劇アーティストであるセシリア・B・ガルチョによって聴衆に朗読された。この書籍は、世界中の子どもたちに偉大な指導者を紹介するため、マグサイサイ賞受賞者の生涯を扱ったシリーズの一環である。 財団は、アリヤ代表とフィリピン・イスラムと民主主義センターのアミナ・ラスル＝ベルナルド会長を招き、「異宗教間の調和と共通の人間性に関する議論」を開催した。アルジャジーラのジャーナリストであるジャメラ・アリンドガンが司会を務めた。議論は主要宗教間における宗教的調和と対話の重要性や、宗教的調和の促進におけるダライ・ラマ法王の役割と貢献に焦点を当てた。登壇者らは、中国共産党政権が無神論でありながら宗教に介入し、宗教的弾圧を正当化するための宗教法を制定している実態について議論した。 アリヤ代表は、ファー・イースタン大学とフィリピン大学アジアセンターでそれぞれ講演を行い、学生や教職員とチベット問題、ダライ・ラマ法王の使命、両国の関係について意見を交わした。学生たちに対し、チベットの政治史や中国共産党による不法占領の経緯を説明し、1960年代初頭の国連総会におけるチベット問題の審議でフィリピンの国民と政府が示した支援に謝意を表した。さらに、学生たちに向けてグローバルな視点を持つよう促し、世界の平和と調和に対するフィリピンの貢献の可能性について語った。学生からは、ダライ・ラマの転生、中道アプローチ、国連の役割などについて質問が寄せられた。講演の様子はこちら。 ファー・イースタン大学のレックス・ロノラ教授は、チベット問題に関する有益な講演を行った代表に謝意を表した。フィリピン大学アジアセンター学部長のノエル・クリスチャン・モラティラ博士とアリエル・ロペス教授は、チベット問題に関する多角的な講演に対して感謝を述べ、アリヤ代表に感謝状を贈呈した。両大学は、インドの中央チベット政権（CTA）の情報・国際関係省（DIIR）およびチベット政策研究所（TPI）を通じてチベット問題に関する書籍を寄贈してくれたチベットハウス・ジャパンに謝意を表明した。 8月25日、アリヤ代表はフィリピン・イスラムと民主主義センターのアミナ・ラスル＝ベルナルドとともに、ポッドキャスト番組「She Talks Peace」に出演し、ダライ・ラマ法王、チベットの平和的な闘争、世界へのメッセージをテーマに議論を行った。質問に対し、アリヤ代表はダライ・ラマ法王のマルクス主義に対する見解、慈悲、中道アプローチ、そしてモンゴルの元朝、中国の明朝、満州の清朝の時代にチベットが平和と調和の促進にいかに貢献したかを説明した。また、信教の自由の侵害や、中国およびその支配地域における主要宗教の指導者選出に対する中国の強引な介入について視聴者に伝えた。 8月27日、フィリピン国会議事堂の儀典官はアリヤ代表とタシ・ヤンゾム事務局長に対し、議事堂の公式案内を行った。その後、エウヘニオ・ペレス・ラウンジにおいて、エイドリアン・アマトン、ルーファス・ロドリゲス、ダダ・イスムラ、ペルシ・センダナの各下院議員が両名を迎え、最近の「中国民族団結進歩促進法」や殉国者ロブガ・ランゼンの焼身自殺について協議した。また、チベット仏教機関の信教の自由と自治を保護するため議員らが提案した議会法案や、両国議会間の議員連盟の設立についても話し合われた。チベット亡命議会のドルマ・ツェリング・テイカン議長からの、「中国民族団結進歩促進法」の過酷さを訴える嘆願書が議員らに提出された。 8日間にわたる日程は8月28日に締めくくられた。ダライ・ラマ法王日本・東アジア代表部事務所のタシ・ヤンゾム事務局長がアリヤ代表に同行し、写真展や講演会、書籍の配布の調整を補佐した。 ――ダライ・ラマ法王日本・東アジア代表部事務所による報告
