title: Statement of the Kashag on the 49th-day of the Passing of the Late Martyr Lobga Rangzen
author: OOT - DC
content: Today marks the Seventh Week (49th-day) of the self-immolation and passing of the martyr Lobsang Palden, popularly known as Lobga Rangzen. He sacrificed his life on July 2, 2026, in front of the United Nations Headquarters in New York City, United States, leaving behind a final testament stating that his action was undertaken in protest against the Chinese Communist Party’s policies and its systematic eradication of the Tibetan identity in Tibet, while calling on all Tibetans to unite and campaign for Tibet’s independence. In observance of the 49th-Day, the Kashag and the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile today, are jointly organising this official solidarity prayer service and peace march to express our deep condolences and respect to the late Lobga Rangzen and all those Tibetans who have sacrificed their lives for the cause of Tibet. We express our strong opposition to the Chinese Communist Party’s implementation of repressive policies in Tibet, particularly the so-called “Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress”. Immediately upon receiving news of the Lobga Rangzen’s self-immolation protest, the Office of Tibet, Washington, D.C., coordinated with the International Campaign for Tibet in convening an urgent online meeting to disseminate verified information to media outlets and instructed Tibetan associations across North America to organise solidarity prayer services. Simultaneously, a request was made through the Office of His Holiness the Dalai Lama, to seek His Holiness’ prayers for the late Lobga Rangzen. The message from the Office of His Holiness the Dalai Lama was relayed to the immediate family members. Furthermore, on behalf of the Kashag, Kalon Kunga Tashi of the Department of Security visited the Phuntsok De-zhi community hall of the New York & New Jersey Tibetan Association that very night to extend our heartfelt condolences. In the official public statement issued on July 3rd, the Sikyong said: “ The unfolding genocide inside Tibet and the enforcement of the draconian ‘ Ethnic Unity and Progress Law ’ on 1 July are what drove Lobga Rangzen to this tragic decision.” An official prayer service was organised that day. To draw international attention to the Chinese government’s ongoing policy of eradicating the Tibetan identity, 157 Tibetans inside Tibet have been known to have self-immolated since 2009, out of which 136 died, 9 have survived, and the status of 12 remains unknown. In exile, including the late Lobga Rangzen, 11 Tibetans have self-immolated, of which 9 died and 2 survived. Not a single brave Tibetan who self-immolated—whether inside Tibet or in exile—ever harmed the lives or property of others. Rather, they sacrificed their own precious lives with the sole motivation of drawing the attention of the Chinese government and the international community to the plight of the Tibetan people. The Special Tibetan General Meeting on September 28, 2012, recognised self-immolation as the highest form of nonviolent act of protest and passed a resolution urging “ all Tibetans to preserve their precious human lives henceforth. ” The Kashag reiterates its appeal to all Tibetans to remain steadfast in serving the Tibetan cause throughout their lives.” Following the tragic death of the late Lobga Rangzen, Tibetans and friends of Tibet around the world continue to hold various peaceful commemorative events in his honour and protest the Chinese government. We express our heartfelt gratitude and deep appreciation to all media outlets for their widespread coverage of these campaigns and to everyone involved for their steadfast expressions of solidarity and support. The Kashag appeals to the Tibetans both inside and outside Tibet to stay vigilant, prudent and united in resisting the policies of the Chinese government aimed at eradicating the Tibetan identity. The sinister intent behind the Chinese Communist Party’s so-called “Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress”, implemented on July 1, 2026, includes: Erosion of Tibetan Language: The Chinese government has placed nearly one million Tibetan children into colonial-style residential schools, forcing them to learn Chinese and adopt a Chinese identity while demanding absolute loyalty to the Chinese Communist Party. This education system strips away their right to grow up within their own culture and learn their mother tongue. Even private study of the Tibetan language during summer and winter vacations is prohibited. Furthermore, this legislation mandates Chinese as the medium of instruction from preschool, eliminating environments for using the Tibetan language in government offices and severely restricting the scope of Tibetan language. Distortion of Tibetan History and Identity: The legislation directs the Chinese central government to conduct “concentrated and diverse forms of publicity and educational activities to forge a strong sense of community of the Chinese nation ( Zhonghua Minzu ).” Under the guise of “ethnic unity”, this legislation also authorises intensified control and surveillance over the way of life, gatherings, and expressions of opinion of the Tibetan people, thus establishing a legal pretext to punish even minor cultural preservation efforts. Forced Cultural Assimilation at the Grassroots Level: By ordering to conduct traditional practices such as weddings and funerals as per “public order and good customs” and to incorporate “consciousness of the common identity of the Chinese nation” into grassroots village regulations, Tibet’s unique culture and traditions are being forcibly assimilated. Sinicisation of Tibetan Buddhism: For years, the Chinese Communist Party has exercised total control over the properties, administration, and education of Tibetan monasteries while politicising the recognition of reincarnated Lamas. The provisions of this legislation further demand religious sites to “adhere to the direction of Sinicising religion,” thereby undermining the authentic spiritual tradition of Tibetan Buddhism developed over thousands of years and converting it into a tool for communist ideology and political compliance. Ethnic Integration: By promoting a “social environment of mutual integration,” implementing specific “measures regarding housing and population management, strengthening service platforms for cross-regional population transfers, supporting cross-regional recruitment between higher education institutions in ethnic and non-ethnic areas, and encouraging cadres to go to grassroots ethnic regions, the Chinese government is pushing intermarriage to reduce Tibetans into minority in their own homeland. Technological Surveillance: Ethnic affairs are being integrated into the overall “social governance mechanism.” Supported by technology such as AI surveillance, electronic ID tracking, facial recognition, GPS location systems, DNA profiling, iris scanning, and grid-based social management systems, every aspect of an individual’s daily life and movement is being strictly monitored and controlled. Political and Social Coercion: All economic and social development projects are contingent upon “firmly forging the consciousness of the common identity of the Chinese nation,” “safeguarding national unity,” and “opposing separatism.” By combining economic incentives with political intimidation, Tibetans are subjected to forced assimilation into the dominant Han society. Political Vetting of Tibetan Cadres: Cadres or entities failing to strictly implement these regulations face investigations and criminal prosecution. Since the recruitment, selection, deployment, and management of cadres must undergo political vetting, Tibetan cadres are targeted as potential offenders. Simply failing to “strictly enforce” the law—let alone causing harm to “ethnic unity”—is deemed a criminal offence, forcing Tibetan cadres to live in constant fear under this regulation day and night. Violation of Autonomy Rights: The legislation denies even the nominal rights and authority to establish local autonomous bodies, formulate and enact local autonomous regulations guaranteed under the Chinese constitution and the Regional Ethnic Autonomy Law by declaring to “uphold and improve the structure of ethnic work with the Party committee’s unified leadership, government management in accordance with law, and in which the United Front Work Department takes the lead in coordination, the ethnic work departments perform their duties, all departments join forces to cooperate, and the whole society participates, to improve the ethnic work coordination mechanism.” Establishment of Extraterritorial Jurisdiction: By asserting legal accountability against overseas individuals or organisations that undermine the implementation of this legislation or engage in ethnic separatist activities, the Chinese Communist Party seeks to bring Tibetans abroad, supporters of other oppressed peoples under Chinese government’s rule, and critics of these regulations under its extraterritorial legal jurisdiction. In short, whether the objectives of this law succeed in the long run depends on how Tibetans inside and outside Tibet resist this sinister strategy and the extent to which the international community supports the truth and the just cause of the Tibetan people. We appeal to the Tibetans in exile living in free countries to conduct various campaigns non-violently, lawfully, and with dignity. Starting from our households, Tibetans both inside and outside Tibet must make greater efforts to preserve Tibet’s unique religion, culture, language, and traditions to counter the Chinese government’s policies aimed at eradicating Tibetan identity. We appeal to Governments and Parliaments of free nations around the world to confront the Chinese government’s implementation of genocidal policies in Tibet through its blatant violation of international law and global order. We urge the international community to recognise the Sino-Tibetan conflict as an unresolved international legal issue and not an internal matter of China. And we seek your support in the resumption of Sino-Tibetan dialogue based on the mutually beneficial Middle-Way Approach policy without preconditions. We also request the think tanks and media organisations to conduct fair, objective analyses and accurate reporting. We also urge the authorities of the Chinese government to stop acting against the progress of human society, cease clinging solely to the perpetuation of their power, and immediately halt policies aimed at eradicating the identities of other non-Chinese nationalities. The Central Tibetan Administration remains firmly committed to pursuing resolution of the Sino-Tibetan conflict based on the Middle-Way Approach policy unanimously adopted by the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile. Holding the courageous spirit of the Tibetans who sacrificed their lives for our cause deep in our hearts, we hold an unyielding pledge to continue working tirelessly so that their sacrifices do not go in vain. In conclusion, we offer our deepest condolences and solidarity to the family members and relatives of the late Lobga Rangzen and all the other Tibetan martyrs who sacrificed their lives for Tibet. We pray that they may be embraced by the supreme compassionate Chenrezig (Avalokiteshvara) and be reborn as Tibetans to continue serving the cause of Tibet. Kashag August 20, 2026 ……………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………………… * Disclaimer: This document is an English translation of the original Tibetan text. In the event of any discrepancies, ambiguity, or conflict between the two versions, the original Tibetan text shall prevail as the final and authoritative version.

title: Central Tibetan Administration Marks India’s 80th Independence Day
author: OOT - DC
content: Dharamshala: On the occasion of the 80th Independence Day of India, the Central Tibetan Administration (CTA) observed a brief ceremony at Gangchen Kyishong on 15 August 2026 to commemorate the historic occasion and express solidarity with the people of India. The ceremony was attended by the heads of the three pillars of the Central Tibetan Administration, Kalon (Minister), Members of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile (TPiE), Secretaries, senior officials and staff of various departments of the CTA. The ceremony commenced with the hoisting of the Indian national flag by Sikyong Penpa Tsering, followed by the rendition of the Indian national anthem. Addressing the media on the occasion, Sikyong Penpa Tsering expressed gratitude to the Government and people of India for their longstanding support and hospitality towards the Tibetan people. He said that the participation of the CTA leadership, dignitaries and staff in the flag-hoisting ceremony and singing the Indian national anthem was a meaningful expression of solidarity with the people of India. Reflecting on India’s struggle for independence, Sikyong said the occasion serves as a reminder to Tibetans outside – the value of freedom and democracy, particularly as Tibetans inside Tibet continue to face a critical situation under the rule of the People’s Republic of China (PRC). He noted that India’s independence was achieved through generations of struggle and the sacrifices which will serve as a source of inspiration and hope for Tibetans. Sikyong recalled the sacrifices of Tibetan freedom fighters, including the recent self-immolation of Lobga Rangzen, who made the ultimate sacrifice for the cause of Tibet. He said that while such sacrifices may not bring immediate responses, the courage and sacrifices of those who have given their lives for Tibet will remain part of world history and be remembered by future generations. He reaffirmed that the Tibetan people will continue their peaceful struggle for freedom while expressing their deep appreciation to the Government and people of India for their continued support. In response to questions from the media, Sikyong Penpa Tsering commended the CTA and the TPiE for their plans to hold an official prayer service in Dharamshala on 20 August 2026, commemorating the 49th day since the passing of Lobga Rangzen. Photo: Office of Tibet, Geneva Bern — The Tibetan community in Switzerland and Liechtenstein has launched a week of peaceful rally and solidarity walk from the Swiss Federal Parliament (Bundeshaus) in Bern to the Embassy of the People's Republic of China in Zurich, from March 4 to 10, 2026. The aim is to raise public awareness of human rights issues in Tibet and to call the Chinese government for transparency, respect for human rights, and compliance with legal standards in Tibetan regions. According to the Office of Tibet, Geneva, on March 4, 2026, the Tibetan Community of Switzerland and Liechtenstein has inaugurated a week-long peaceful rally and solidarity walk in Bern, they will walk till march 10th, 2026, the Tibetan National Uprising Day, from the Swiss Federal Parliament (Bundeshaus) in Bern to the Embassy of the People’s Republic of China in Zurich. Around 15 participants, aged between the ages of 35 and 75, represent intergenerational commitment and unity. This event, based on non-violence, dignity, and constructive dialogue, aims to raise public awareness of humanitarian concerns in Tibet and call for transparency, respect for human rights, and compliance with legal standards in Tibetan regions. Representative Thinley Chukki, the Office of Tibet, Geneva, addressed the participants at the launch and she saud,''Today, as we gather in front of the Swiss Parliament, I thank our guest of honour, a Member of Parliament, for inaugurating this peace march. This march coincides with the 90th birthday of His Holiness the Dalai Lama and seeks to draw global attention to the suffering of Tibetans in Tibet. Over one million Tibetan children face forced residential schooling, and in 2024 alone, around 650,000 Tibetans were effected by the forced labour programmes according to the UN reports. Infrastructure projects and dams have displaced nearly one million Tibetans, depriving them of their livelihoods." "We call on the international community to recognise these violations and extend their support. I thank all participants for dedicating seven days of their lives to this cause. May our efforts advance freedom in Tibet, a peaceful resolution of the Sino-Tibetan conflict, and the long life of His Holiness the Dalai Lama," she added. Katharina Prelicz-Huber, Member of the National Council of Switzerland, expressed her support, conveying the solidarity of the Tibetan Parliamentary Group and providing a message to be delivered on 10 March, 2026, marking the 67th anniversary of the Tibetan National Uprising Day. The letter was signed by co-presidents Councillor of States Diana Moser, National Councillor Leonore Borges, National Councillor Nick Gucker, National Councillor Fabian Molina, and Maya Graf, Councillor of States. According to the report, beyond Tibet, the march carries a universal message: in a world affected by war, conflict, and human suffering, peace, dialogue, and non-violence remain essential. Inspired by His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama, Tenzin Gyatso, the Tibetan Community emphasises that lasting solutions come through respect, understanding, and peaceful negotiation. They said that the march from Bern to Zurich stands as both a call for justice in Tibet and a symbolic gesture of solidarity with all peoples affected by war and instability worldwide. Photo: TYC New Delhi — The Tibetan Youth Congress (TYC) organised a strong protest outside the Embassy of the People's Republic of China in New Delhi on June 7, 2026. The demonstrators protested against the Chinese government's ongoing political repression in Tibet and the implementation of the so-called "ethnic unity" law, while also paying tribute to the sacrifice of Tibetan patriot Lobga Rangzen, who sacrificed his life for the cause of Tibet. The Tibetan Youth Congress also sent an open letter to the Embassy of People's Republic of China in New Delhi on the same day and they said,"This is not merely a letter. It is a message carried by the final sacrifice of Tibetan patriot Lobga Rangzen, whose body was engulfed in flames because our homeland had been occupied and our people deprived of their freedom. His last act was not one of despair, it was one of resistance. he raised the Tibetan National Flag and he stood on fire, and declared to the world: "Free Tibet, China Out of Tibet." "Rangzen Lobga sacrificed his life because, he view that the root cause of the Tibetan tragedy is simple: China occupied our country, we lost our independence and the continued political control exercised by the so-called People's Republic of China over Tibet. He sacrificed himself for the cause of Tibet and its Independence because decades of political repression, cultural destruction, restrictions on religious freedom, transnational repression, and now the implementation of the so-called "Ethnic Unity Law." "You call it a law of unity. In reality you are trying to legalize the genocide, a legal procedure design to erase the identity of oppressed people. A law that weakens a nation's language, religion, culture, and history cannot be called unity. Unity cannot be imposed through assimilation. Unity cannot be manufactured through fear. Unity without freedom is not unity at all. "For almost seven decades, the so-called Chinese Communist government has attempted to suppress and silence Tibetans inside Tibet and across the world. Military occupation, surveillance, imprisonment, propaganda, misinformation, disinformation campaigns, and enormous financial investment to reshape historical narratives, But failed to extinguish the Tibetan people's aspiration for freedom. "Despite immense pressure, Tibetans have not disappeared. They have become more resilient. Every attempt to erase our identity has strengthened our determination to preserve it. Every effort to silence us has inspired new voices to speak. Every sacrifice has produced a new generation committed to carrying forward the cause of Tibet. "The oppressor dream of creating "one big China" through coercion will remain only that a dream. so as long as Tibetans continue to preserve their national identity and seek justice. Ideas cannot be imprisoned. History cannot be rewritten simply through repetition. National identity cannot be erased by decree. "Rangzen Lobga made his message unmistakably clear: "the root cause of the Tibetan issue is that Tibet lost its independence after China took control of our land." "The Tibetan Youth Congress has never wavered in its position. We firmly stands and believe that the Tibetan people have the right to determine their own future, and our mission remains unchanged: to reclaim our country, Tibet, from the foreign occupation. "This is perhaps one of the most important moments for the so-called Government of the People's Republic of China to resume sincere and meaningful dialogue with the Tibetan Government in Exile, Dialogue is not a sign of weakness. It is the mark of confidence. Nations secure in their legitimacy do not fear conversation. History has shown that governments can suppress protests, imprison individuals, and control information, but they cannot permanently extinguish a people's aspiration for freedom and dignity. "The world has changed. Information travels across borders in seconds. Voices cannot be silenced as they once were. Attempts to conceal injustice face greater international scrutiny than ever before. Rangzen Lobga's sacrifice will not never be a forgotten chapter despite will be the source of motivation. It should serve as a warning that unresolved political conflicts continue to carry profound human consequences. "We therefore call upon the so-called Government of the People's Republic of China to end its illegal occupation of Tibet and respect the Tibetan people's inherent right to self-determination. "The Chinese government must recognize the legitimate aspiration of the Tibetan people and restore Tibet's independence. Lasting peace and stability cannot be achieved through repression, forced assimilation, or military control, but only by ending occupation and respecting the will of the Tibetan people. We urge China to choose justice over oppression, freedom over domination, and peace over continued confrontation. "History will judge not only those who resisted oppression, but also those who had the opportunity to pursue peace and chose otherwise. Act now or regret later," the Tibetan activists of Tibetan Youth Congress said. Photo: File Dharamshala — The Chinese authorities have demolished thousands of residences of Tibetan monks and nuns in Larung Gar, the world’s largest Tibetan Buddhist institute, since 2001. The latest wave of demolitions began in mid-July and is set to destroy 1,060 dwellings of monks and nuns. These demolitions took place following the implementation of China’s new law, so-called the “Law on Ethnic Unity and Progress,” which came into effect on July 1, 2026. According to these sources, on July 13, 2026, Chinese authorities began to demolish at least 1,060 dwellings belonging to monks and nuns at the Larung Five Sciences Buddhist Academy, better known as Larung Gar (monastery), located in Sertar County in eastern Tibet; at least six dwellings were demolished till July 15, 2026. These actions occurred following the implementation of so-called China's new “Law on Ethnic Unity and Progress” on July 1, 2026, which targets the Tibetan language, identity, culture, and religion as part of a policy of Sinicization and imposes the assimilation of Tibetans into Chinese culture through public institutions. "The demolitions in Larung Gar began around July 13, 2026, and are being carried out at night, which is seen as a tactic by the authorities to prevent public documentation, media coverage, and satellite monitoring. As of July 15, 2026, six dwellings had been demolished, and Chinese authorities continue to destroy the residences; they have targeted at least 1,060 dwellings belonging to monks and nuns for demolition as part of this latest phase of demolitions," the sources said. In 2001, Chinese authorities launched their first large-scale demolition and forced eviction operations at the Larung Gar Buddhist Academy, targeting thousands of monastic dwellings. Since then, the Chinese government has intermittently resumed its destruction activities, notably launching a massive demolitionoperationin July 2016 that reportedly resulted in theexpulsionof more than 4,800 monks and nuns and the demolition of 4,700 dwellings; the most recent wave targeted at least 1,060 dwellings. The the Serta Larung Five Science Buddhist Academy was founded by Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok, Tibetan lama and great scholar in 1980 and has grown to the point where, it hosts between 10,000 and 40,000 residents. It is home to monks, nuns, and students from Tibet and China, as well as from other countries such as South Korea, Singapore, and Malaysia, while tens of thousands of people around the world study Buddhism through online courses taught by Sodargye Rinpoche, a prominent khenpo from Larung Gar. Despite the restrictions imposed by Chinese authorities on Tibetan Buddhism under Chinese occupation, Larung Gar has greatly contributed to the spread of this religion as well as to the preservation and international dissemination of Tibetan culture. Hundreds of eminent Buddhist scholars and practitioners have been educated at Larung Gar. Since the Chinese government began systematically demolishing Larung Gar, the European Parliament, United Nations special rapporteurs, numerous countries, and human rights organisations, including Human Rights have officially condemned the Chinese government’s destruction of Larung Gar and called on it to put an end to these demolitions. "China’s actions, in no doubts, constitute a gross violation of international human rights law, as well as its own Constitution, which obligates China to respect and protect the cultural, social, and religious rights of the Tibetan people. Instead, by forcing mass evictions of Tibetan monastic communities and replacing Tibetan self-governance with direct Chinese Communist Party administration, China is actively dismantling the very fabric of Tibetan life. The human toll of the Larung Gar crackdown that took place in 2016 and 2017 has been disastrous, resulting in profound psychological trauma and tragic suicides, such as the deaths of Tibetan nuns Tsering Dolma and Semgha amid the 2016 demolitions," the UN, EU, and the Human Rights Desk, Tibet Advocacy Section, DIIR, Central Tibetan Administration said. China-Tibet: The one-thing you need to know: Over the past 70 decades, there has been ongoing political repression, social discrimination, economic marginalization, environmental destruction, and cultural assimilation, particularly due to Chinese migration to Tibet which is fueling intense resentment among the people of occupied Tibet. The communist-totalitarian state of China began its invasion of Tibet in 1949, reaching complete occupation of the country in 1959. Since that time, more than 1.2 million people, 20% of the nation's population of six million, have died as a direct result of China's invasion and occupation. In addition, over 99% of Tibet's six thousand religious monasteries, temples, and shrines, have been looted or decimated resulting in the destruction of hundreds of thousands of sacred Buddhist scriptures. Until 1949, Tibet was an independent Buddhist nation in the Himalayas which had little contact with the rest of the world. It existed as a rich cultural storehouse of the Mahayana and Vajrayana teachings of Buddhism. Religion was a unifying theme among the Tibetans -- as was their own language, literature, art, and world view developed by living at high altitudes, under harsh conditions, in a balance with their environment. Tibetans, supporters of the Tibetan cause, and human rights advocates expressed their deep sorrow and called for freedom and justice for Tibet. A mass protest by Tibetans took place in front of the United Nations headquarters in New York—the site where Tibetan patriot Lobga Rangzen had set himself on fire to protest the Chinese government's repression of the Tibetan people, language, religion, and culture, to demand independence for Tibet, June 2,2026. Tibetans held candlelight vigils in tribute to Lobga Rangzen, in New York, Toronto, Paris, Sydney, Dharamshala, and many other places on June 3, 2026. Tibetans held candlelight vigils in tribute to Lobga Rangzen, in New York, Toronto, Paris, Sydney, Dharamshala, and many other places on June 3, 2026. Hundreds of Tibetans and Tibet Supporters filled up the Leh Market and held a candlelight vigil in tribute to Lobga Rangzen, a Tibetan independence activist who set himself on fire outside the United Nations headquarters in New York on June 2, 2026. He carried out this act to protest the Chinese government's repressive policies in Tibet and to demand independence for Tibet. On June 5, 2026, a mass protest by Tibetans took place in front of the United Nations headquarters in New York—the site where Tibetan patriot Lobga Rangzen had set himself on fire to protest the Chinese government's repression of the Tibetan people, language, religion, and culture—to demand independence for Tibet, June 2,2026. Tibetans also held a memorial service for Lobga Rangzen at the Tibetan Community Center in New York, followed by his funeral on June 6, 2026. All the Tibetans present were deeply saddened and overcome with grief by the passing of Lobga Rangzen, an independence activist of Tibet. Sikyong Penpa Tsering of the Central Tibetan Administration expressed deep sorrow over the self-immolation of a Tibetan activist, Lobga Rangzen (Lobsang Palden), in front of the UN Headquarters in New York City on 2 July 2026. Sikyong said,"I am deeply saddened by the devastating news of Lobga Rangzen's (Lobsang Palden) self-immolation in front of the UN Headquarters in New York City on July 2, 2026. In a video message posted hours prior, he made it clear that this ultimate sacrifice was undertaken for the Tibetan national cause. While we honor his devotion, human life is precious and must be preserved to serve the long-term struggle for Tibet." "On behalf of the Central Tibetan Administration (CTA), I earnestly urge all fellow Tibetans to cherish your lives. The unfolding genocide inside Tibet and the enforcement of the draconian "Ethnic Unity and Progress Law" on July 1 are what drove Lobga Rangzen la to this tragic decision. He joins at least 157 Tibetans inside Tibet who have offered their lives to draw global attention to the brutal repression endured under Chinese rule," Sikyong said. "Our deepest condolences go out to Lobga Rangzen la's family, friends, and the entire Tibetan community. On behalf of the CTA and the Tibetan people, I solemnly pledge that we will carry the spirit of these sacrifices in our hearts and work relentlessly so they are not in vain. I urgently call upon Tibetans in exile, world governments, and international human rights institutions to recognize the severe crisis inside Tibet, to stand up, and to speak out at this critical moment in our history," Sikyong concluded. United Nations Spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric expressed sadness over the self-immolation that took place outside UN headquarters, emphasising that minorities—regardless of the country—must be respected and feel as part of whole. Photo:Tenzin Wangdu Rangzen Dharamshala — More than 60 Tibetans shaved their heads in solidarity with Tibetan martyr Lobga Rangzen and all those who have sacrificed their lives for a free Tibet; Lobga Rangzen had set himself on fire in front of the United Nations headquarters to protest against China's illegal occupation of Tibet, its oppressive actions in the region, and the genocidal policies implementing in Tibet. This Head-shaving movement took place in front of United Nations headquarters, in New York, on July 30, 2026 and it is orgainsed by 19th Regional Tibetan Youth Congress of NY&NY. They said,"This act of sacrifice is a symbol of our unwavering commitment to justice, truth, and the independence of our nation. We call upon the United Nations to uphold the principles it was founded on and stand for justice. The world cannot remain silent." They collected the shaved hair and wrote "Justice for Lobga Rangzen" to commemorate Lhogar Rangren's sacrifice for a free and independent Tibet and to seek justice for him. They also shouted slogans such as "Justice for Lhogar Rangren," "Free Tibet," "China, out of Tibet now," and "United Nations, wake up" in front of the United Nations headquarters in New York. Following the head-shaving movement, hundreds of Tibetans gathered in front of the United Nations headquarters in New York, the site where Tibetan martyr Lobga Rangzen self-immolated. They protested China's forced invasion of Tibet, destruction of Tibetan Buddhist monasteries, environmental damage, and the killing of over two million Tibetans, and its continued repressive and harsh policies against Tibetans, Tibetan culture, language, freedom of expression, religion, and belief, including the arrest, torture, and imprisonment of any Tibetan exercising their basic rights. During their protest, they held up signs that read: "UN, when will you stop being silenced by China?", "UN, how many more lives do you need?", "Tibet belongs to Tibetans, not China", "Communist China, hands off Tibet", We want an independent for Tibet", "Protect Tibet's Faith, Culture and Nation","Lobga Rangzen is a US citizen, we want justice". Jamphel Choesang, President of 19th Regional Tibetan Youth Congress New York/New Jersey addressed the gathering and said, "Dear Tibetan brothers and sisters, Today, I stand before you not only as the President of the 19th Regional Tibetan Youth Congress New York/New Jersey, but as a fellow Tibetan whose heart carries the same hope, pain, and unwavering love for our homeland. "Our martyrs gave everything they had for Tibet. They did not sacrifice for themselves—they sacrificed for all of us, for future generations, and for the dream of a free and independent Tibet. Their courage must never be forgotten, and their sacrifices must never be in vain. "Our beloved Pawo Lobga Rangzen la made the ultimate sacrifice to awaken the conscience of the world and to remind us that Tibet’s struggle is far from over. His message was clear: never give up on Tibet. "Today, I humbly call upon every Tibetan brother and sister: please stand up for our country. Join our protests whenever you can. Raise your voice for justice. Your presence matters. Every person standing together sends a powerful message that Tibet lives in our hearts and that we will never surrender our identity, our culture, or our dream of freedom. "Let us stand united—not divided. Let us work together as one family, one community, and one nation. When we support one another with respect, compassion, and determination, there is nothing stronger than our unity. "The responsibility to continue this movement belongs to every one of us. Whether young or old, student or professional, every effort counts. Every protest, every prayer, every act of service, and every voice raised for Tibet keeps the flame of our martyrs burning brightly. "Let us honor Pawo Lobga Rangzen la and all our martyrs not only with words, but through our actions. Let us continue the path they showed us with courage, discipline, and unwavering commitment. "We call upon the international community and the United Nations to hear the voices of the Tibetan people and to seek justice for Pawo Lobga Rangzen la. His sacrifice deserves to be remembered, and the Tibetan people’s aspirations deserve to be heard. "Together, let us pledge that we will never allow our martyrs’ sacrifices to be forgotten. We will continue to stand for truth, justice, and the freedom of Tibet until the day our nation is free." Photo:file Dharamshala — Shilong-led northeast India Tibetan People's Movement held a press conference at the Guwahatu Press Club, to address the ongoing human rights crisis in Tibet, which led to the self-immolation of Tibetan activist Lobga Rangzen, in front of UN headquarters in New York, on July 2, 2026. They told the media about who is Tibetan independent activist Lobga Rangzen and why he self-immolated in front of UN headquarters in New York. They further recalled China's invasion of Tibet and denounced the Chinese government's eradication of Tibetan language, identity, culture, and religion in the name of so-called China's “Law on Ethnic Unity and Progress"; finally they rejected the law by tearing the law paper, in front of reporters. Shilong-led northeast India Tibetan People's Movement, planned to organise a large peaceful protest in Guwahati (Assam) on July 29, 2026, to protest against China's so-called "Ethnic Unity Law" and demand freedom, justice, and respect for human rights in Tibet. Tibetans from various northeastern states—including Dimapur (Nagaland), Tawang (Arunachal Pradesh), Tezpur (Assam), Shillong (Meghalaya), and Guwahati (Assam)—were set to participate; however, due to flooding in Assam, the demonstration had to be postponed, and a press conference was held instead on the originally scheduled date of July 29, 2026. Two former members of Tibetan Parliament-in-exile, Tsering Dolma and Yangchen Dolkar, Tenzin sangmo, media coordinator and Youndoung, secretary of Shilong-led northeast India Tibetan People's Movement held the press conference. The statement of the Shilong-led northeast India Tibetan People's Movement said," Lobga Rangzen, a 52-year-old Tibetan activist, died after a self-immolation protest he carried out in front of the UN headquarters in New York City on July 2, 2026. He called for the restoration of Tibet's independence and spoke against the imposition of China's "Ethnic Unity and Progress Law" that went into force on July 1 in Tibet. Tibetans reject this law as it is designed to legitimise the imposition of sinicization policies in Tibet. Tibetans are not an ethnic minority of China to be subjected to its ethnic unity law in the name of unity and progress. "In 1950, the People's Liberation Army entered Tibet, fundomentally changing the course of Tibetan history. Following the 1959 Tibetan Uprising, His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama and approximately 80,000 Tibetans fled into exile in India. Since China's military occupation of Tibet, Tibetans have lived under policies that many governments, UN experts and international human rights organisations say have severely restricted fundamental rights. "More than 170 Tibetans have self-immolated since 2009, pealing in 2012 with 85 self-immolations in one year. All the self-immolators unanimously called for freedom in Tibet, the protection of Tibetan Identity, the return of His Holiness the Dalai lama to Tibet, and unity among Tibetans. His Holiness the 14th Dalal Lama and the exile government continue to make efforts toward peaceful resolution of the Sino-Tibetan conflict through its "Middle Way Approach". However, China has only turned a cold shoulder to the proposals and responds with rhetoric that undermines the spirit of dialogue. It has put the Tibetans in a difficult position of experiencing the worsening human rights situation in Tibet, while watching China intensify its hold on Tibet. Self-Immolations don't occur in a vacuum, but as a result of deep-seated anguish and exhaustion of tangible recourse. "On July 1, 2026, China's "Ethnic Unity and Progress Law" come into force. According to the Chinese government, the law "promotes national unity". However, eight UN human rights experts and international human rights organisations have warned that it further institutionalizes policies affecting the linguistic, cultural and religious rights of ethnic minorities. There are major factual inaccuracies in the law and in the UN response: • Tibet is not part of China to be absorbed into the project of national unity• Tibetans are minoritised by the Chinese occupation and are not one of the ethnic minority groups China claims to constitute.• China is ethnically Han Chinese dominated, with no historical, cultural, racial, linguistic or political association with the Tibetans, except as the dominast race of the colonising power. "On the ground in Tibet, the law has real time impact on education, language, religion and cultural rights as it mandates cultural integration. The single Chinese national identity it promotes includes provisions with extraterritorial application, raising concerns that it could exacerbate the patterns of transnational repression against individuals and organisations globally. For many Tibetans, the law is seen not as a new policy but as the formal codification of decades of assimilation measures through instrumentalisation of law. "Why should India and northeast care for Tibet. The Tibetan Plateau forms much of the strategic frontier between India and China. Since China's occupation of Tibet, the Himalayan region has become one of Asia's most heavily militarised borders. China has escalated its territorial claims over Arunachal Pradesh, referring to it as "South Tibet," and maintains unresolved border disputes with India in eastern Ladakh. These disputes have contributed to recurring military tensions, including the 2020 Galwan Valley clash. "For the people of Northeast India, Tibet is not only a human rights issue—it is also an environmental and regional concern. The Brahmaputra (Yarlung Tsangpo) originates on the Tibetan Plateau before flowing through Arunachal Pradesh and Assam, sustaining millions of people. Decisions affecting Tibet's rivers and fragile ecosystem-including dam construction, hydropower stations, water diversion, and mining have implications for communities downstream that constitute two billion people." Photo: File Washington — U.S Senator Jacky Rosen,Jeff Merkley, John Curtis, and Jim Banks, introduced a Bipartisan Resolution on the China's “Ethnic Unity and Progress Law” in US Senate on June 24, 2026. The resolution condemns China’s "Ethnic Unity and Progress Law," which entered into force on 1 July 2026, and calls on Beijing to end abuses against ethnic and religious minorities, as well as campaigns of transnational repression affecting people in the United States. The resolution highlighted human rights violations in Tibet, the forced placement of more than one million Tibetan children in colonial-style boarding schools; it also emphasized that the Chinese authorities are violating the fundamental rights and freedoms guaranteed by the Chinese Constitution and international law. It further detailed how the Chinese Communist government imposes repressive policies—both old and new—on Tibetans in Chinese-occupied Tibet; as well as the Sinicisation of the Tibetan language, culture, and religion; the People’s Republic of China’s attempt to control the reincarnation of His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama of Tibet; and China’s Ethnic Unity Law, which undermines the unity of minority groups. The resolution states, "Condemning the People's Republic of China's Ethnic Unity and Progress Law, concerned with its implications on the rights and freedoms, as well as survival of the identity, of Tibetans, Uyghurs, Mongolians, and other affected communities, and calling on the Government of the People's Republic of China to end its abuses and campaigns of transnational repression that undermine United States sovereignty and threaten the safety and freedoms of people in the United States. "The Constitution of the People's Republic of China guarantees specified rights, including freedom of religious belief and the right of people regarded as minorities to use their own spoken and written languages and preserve their cultural traditions. The People's Republic of China is a State Party to the Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC) and the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (ICESCR) and is a signatory to the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights. "Chinese authorities have systematically imposed policies that displace ethnic and religious minority communities, separate Tibetan and Uyghur children from their families through state-run boarding schools, limit the use of minority languages, curtail religious practice through intrusive state controls, and compel conformity with ideology mandated by the Chinese Communist Party. "The policies of the People's Republic of China have threatened the rights and freedoms of a broad range of communities, including Tibetans, Uyghurs, Mongolians, Christians, and other ethnic and religious groups across China, as well as the people of Hong Kong whose civil liberties and autonomy have been systematically eroded in recent years. "The July 1, 2026, entry into force of the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law of the People's Republic of China institutionalizes and expands coercive assimilation and cultural erasure policies directed toward Tibetans, Uyghurs, Mongolians, Christians, and other groups.The Ethnic Unity and Progress Law codifies the Chinese Communist Party's campaign of "Sinicization," requiring schools, religious institutions, families, media, and cultural organizations to align their activities with Party-mandated ideology. "The Ethnic Unity and Progress Law criminalizes expression deemed to "undermine ethnic unity" or "create ethnic division", the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law contains extraterritorial provisions authorising Chinese authorities to pursue "legal responsibility" for individuals and organizations outside China, which includes United States citizens who "undermine ethnic unity" or challenge the Chinese Communist Party's official historical narratives." "The Ethnic Unity and Progress Law expands state authority over religious institutions in ways that threaten the ability of Tibetan Buddhist leaders to determine matters of religious tradition, including the succession of the Dalai Lama; and the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law represents a grave escalation in the campaign of the People's Republic of China to suppress ethnic, religious, cultural, and linguistic diversity and, when combined with the Chinese Government's expanding campaigns of transnational repression, illegal overseas police operations, and extraterritorial claims of authority, poses a growing threat to the United States and its allies. Resolved, That the Senate-(1) condemns the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law for institutionalizing coercive assimilation, cultural erasure, and ideological control over ethnic and religious minorities in the People's Republic of China;(2) reaffirms support for the fundamental rights and freedoms of Tibetans, Uyghurs, Mongolians, Hui Muslims, Christians, and other ethnic and religious communities in the People's Republic of China;(3) reaffirms the 2021 determination of the United States Department of State that the Government of the People's Republic of China is committing genocide and crimes against humanity against Uyghurs and other predominantly Muslim Turkic people,(4) calls on the Government of the People's Republic of China to repeal the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law;(5) urges the United States Department of State to work with allies and partners, including the European Union, Canada, Japan, Australia, and the United Kingdom, to monitor and report on the impacts of the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law and on going transnational repression carried out by the People's Republic of China;(6) calls on the President to evaluate and consider targeted sanctions under the Global Magnitsky Human Rights Accountability Act (22 U.S.C. 10101et seq.) against individuals and entities responsible for, complicit in, or directly benefiting from gross human rights violations that result from implementing the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law and related laws and policies;(7) recognizes the Dalai Lama and the Central Tibetan Administration for their longstanding commitment to nonviolence and dialogue and reaffirms that, in light of the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law's expansion of state authority over religions institutions, decisions regarding the reincarnation or succession of the Dalai Lama are solely the prerogative of Tibetan Buddhist leaders and the Tibetan people, free from interference by the Government of the People's Republic of China, as outlined in the Tibetan Policy and Support Act of 2020; and(8) calls on the Government of the People's Republic of China to resume dialogue with the Dalai Lama or his representatives in order to hold substantive discussions aimed at resolution of the Sino-Tibetan disputes at an early date, without preconditions. Photo: TPI Dharamshala — Tibetans commemorated the 11th anniversary of the passing of Tulku Tenzin Delek Rinpoche, who was assassinated by the Chinese government. They spoke about Rinpoche’s legacy and paid tribute to his bravery, highlighted Tenzin Delek Rinpoche’s contributions in the fields of education, environmental protection and social welfare; how his patriotic commitment and his work in the service of the community had become a source of growing concern for the authorities of the People’s Republic of China.. The Tulku Tenzin Delek Rinpoche Service Committee and the Tibetan Center for Human Rights and Democracy (TCHRD) organised a memorial event on July 13, 2026, at Norbu House in Dharamsala to mark the 11th anniversary of Tulku Tenzin Delek Rinpoche’s death. Rinpoche was murdered by Chinese authorities on July 12, 2015 in a Chinese prison, for fear of his influence on Tibetan society and for courageously protecting Tibetan religion, culture, language and environment. The event included the launch of a book in English recording the evidence of his assassination. The English translation of Nyima Lhamo’s book, titled > was launched by the Speaker of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile, Dolma Tsering Teykhang. Speaker Dolma Tsering Teykhang, Tenzin Dawa, Director of the TCHRD, Dorjee Rinchen, author of Tenzin Delek Rinpoche’s books, and Geshe Tsering Dorjee, a student of Tenzin Delek Rinpoche, spoke about Rinpoche’s legacy and paid tribute to his courage and bravery, as he is a true representative of Tibetans who protect the Tibetan environment, teach the Tibetan language and culture as well as Buddhism to the people. More than 50 Tibetans from the Dharamsala area participated in this event. > original in Tibetan, told by Nyima Lhamo and written by Dorjee Rinchen,launchedin 2024; the Chinese version,publishedin 2025, was translated by Loya, while the English version >, launched on July 13, 2026, was translated by the Tibetan writer Bhuchung Sonam. The book is about how Tenzin Delek Rinpoche was arrested without any crime, how he suffered in the Chinese prison, how his students and local Tibetans pleaded for his release, how the Chinese authorities shot at peaceful followers and demonstrators, how Tibetans were beaten and arrested by the Chinese authorities and, finally, how he was murdered by the Chinese, and how the Chinese authorities refused to return Rinpoche's body to his family because they feared that the cause of death would become known to the world, how Rinpoche's niece Nyima Lhamo and other Tibetans were detained and tortured, how she tried to immolate herself in front of the Chinese prison etc. Geshe Tsering Dorjee introduced the event by stating that yesterday was the day, Tenzin Delek Rinpoche was murdered by the Chinese authorities while serving his sentence in a Chinese prison on July 12, 2015. “Today, I wanted to remind all of you of the importance of unity among Tibetans, because those were the last words Tenzin Delek Rinpoche spoke to me as I was preparing to go into exile. We must all unite and fight for our cause; one day, we will achieve our freedom,” he said. Author Dorjee Rinchen recounted how Tenzin Delek Rinpoche founded nine monasteries to promote Tibetan Buddhism, built schools for orphans and other children, and protected Tibet’s fragile environment and wildlife from being slaughtered. He also spoke about how the People’s Republic of China attempted to assassinate Tibetans who were influential figures in Tibetan society, such as Tulku Tenzin Delek Rinpoche, Khenchen Jigme Phuntso, and Geshe Sonam Phuntso in Karze, and how the same thing occurred in other Tibetan regions. These are repressive policies carried out by the Chinese Communist government aimed at eliminating Tibetans, along with their culture, identity, and religion. Speaker Dolma Tsering Teykhang spoke about the courage of Tulku Tenzin Delek Rinpoche by recounting how Rinpoche had secretly met with the first fact-finding delegation from the Tibetan government-in-exile, which included Lobsang Samten, the elder brother of His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama. During this meeting, he provided first-hand accounts of the destruction of Lithang Monastery and of the severe restrictions imposed by the People’s Republic of China (PRC) on religious freedom in the region. He also explained how Tenzin Delek Rinpoche had met the 10th Panchen Lama, briefed him in detail on the situation in Lithang and consulted him on the reconstruction of the monasteries at Ngachu and Lithing counties. The Speaker also highlighted Tenzin Delek Rinpoche’s contributions in the fields of education, environmental protection and social welfare; he further explained how his patriotic commitment and his work in the service of the community had become a source of growing concern for the authorities of the People’s Republic of China. Nyima Lhamo, niece of Tenzin Delek Rinpoche said, "Today marks 11 years since the tragic and unjust death of Tulku Tenzin Delek Rinpoche, a revered Tibetan lama, educator, environmentalist, and cultural leader who died under suspicious circumstances after 13 years of imprisonment and relentless torture at the hands of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP)." "His only “crime” was his unwavering commitment to preserving Tibetan religion, identity, and human rights — values that the CCP considers a threat to its authoritarian rule. The CCP feared Rinpoche’s popularity, moral authority, and influence among Tibetans, and thus silenced him through violence and oppression," she added. title: CTA and Tibetans mourn the demise of Kasur Chope Paljor Tsering - Tibet Post International
content: Dharamshala — Central Tibetan Administration and Tibetans mourned the demise of Kasur Chope Paljor Tsering, who devoted more than four decades of dedicated service to His Holiness the Dalai Lama, the Tibetan people, and the Tibetan cause. He has served as the Kalon for Department of Health during the 13th Kashag and served over two decades as the Representative of His Holiness the Dalai Lama in various countries. The former Kalon Chope Paljor Tsering passed away on June 11, 2026 in Australia. Central Tibetan Administration held a prayer service on June 12, 2026, in Dharamshala, to mourn the passing of former Kalon (Kasur) Choepe Paljor Tsering Namru Ringpapo Ntsang. Kasur Chope was born in 1948 in Namru, in the Northern Tibet. Following the Communist Chinese invasion of Tibet, he fled with his family at around the age of ten. The family eventually settled in Pokhara, Nepal. In 1966, he served as the translator during the establishment of the Tashi Ling Tibetan settlement in Pokhara. From 1968 to 1970, he studied in the United Kingdom before returning to Tashi Ling to serve as a teacher and, later, school principal. From 1973, he served as Tibetan Settlement Officer of Dhorpatan, northern Nepal. From 1978 Kasur Chope served at the Office of the Representative of His Holiness the Dalai Lama in Nepal. He was then transferred to the Department of Education in Dharamshala as its Deputy Secretary on April 26, 1982. Returning to Nepal, he served as the Central Tibetan Administration’s Education Officer for Nepal. From May 1986, Kasur Chope served as the Representative of His Holiness the Dalai Lama in Nepal. He went on to serve as Representative for Eastern Europe (1991–1998), for Australasia (1998–2002), and finally for Japan and East Asia (2002–2007). With twenty-one years in the role, he was the longest-serving Representative of His Holiness the Dalai Lama thus far. In 2007, he was unanimously elected to the 13th Kashag (Cabinet) by the Tibetan Parliament in Exile and served as Kalon (Minister) for Department of Health until 2011. In retirement, he continued to work to preserve and promote Tibetan language and culture through the Global Tibet Institute. He also a book named "The Nature of All Things: The Life Story of a Tibetan in Exile" , an autobiography which recounts his childhood in Tibet, life as a refugee and his experiences in serving His Holiness the Dalai Lama, Tibetan people and Tibetan cause. title: US senators call on PRC to rescind the law aimed at erasing the unique identity of the Tibetan - Tibet Post International
content: Washington, D.C. — In a letter addressed to the Chinese ambassador to the United States, U.S. Senators Lindsey Graham and Sheldon Whitehouse expressed their deep concern regarding the “Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress” enacted by the PRC, warning that this law aims to eliminate the distinct identities, religious freedoms, and fundamental rights of Tibetans, Uyghurs, and other ethnic minorities. They further stated that this new law violates the Chinese Constitution and international law, and that it must be repealed. Senators Lindsey O. Graham (Republican) and Sheldon Whitehouse (Democrat) sent a bipartisan letter to Xie Feng, China’s ambassador to the United States, on June 25, 2026. In the letter, they expressed deep concern regarding the “Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress” enacted by the People’s Republic of China, warning that this law aims to eliminate the distinct identities, religious freedoms, and fundamental rights of Tibetans, Uyghurs, and other ethnic minorities. They further stated that this new law violates the Chinese Constitution and international law, and that it must be repealed. The senators stated that they joined the European Parliament in condemning the so-called "Ethic Unity law," which is set to take effect on July 1, 2026 and called on the Chinese government to repeal it or revise it thoroughly. They added that they would closely monitor the Chinese Communist Party’s implementation of the law, particularly its impact on Tibetans, Uyghurs and others. The senators wrote in the letter to China’s ambassador to the United States,"We write with grave concern regarding the troubling implications of the People's Republic of China's new Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress which will enter into force on July 1." "As bipartisan and elected representatives of the U.S. Senate, we join the European Union Parliament in condemning the Law's passage and anticipated implementation. We are closely watching actions the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) takes under the Law and would urge your government to rescind or significantly revise the Law given its ramifications on those beyond the borders of the People's Republic of China and on the protection of distinct identities and human rights of Tibetans, Uyghurs, and other nationalities," they added. "We are extremely concerned about Article 63 of the Law, which states "Organizations and individuals outside the [mainland] territory of the People's Republic of China that commit acts aimed at the People's Republic of China that undermine ethnic unity and progress or create ethnic division are to be pursued for legal responsibility in accordance with law." Please be aware that any attempts to surveil, intimidate, or pressure individuals residing in the United States, under Article 63 or any provision of that Law or any other, constitute an unacceptable violation of U.S. sovereignty," they further said. The US senators said, "We are deeply troubled by the codification of the CCP's longstanding practices to extinguish religious freedom, including restrictions on worship, forced ideological instruction, and pressure on communities to abandon or dilute their faith traditions. These practices affect Tibetan Buddhists, Muslims, Christians, and many others - under the guise of combatting extremism and/or preventing separatism." "We are also alarmed by the law's implications for children's rights, particularly in the state-run boarding schools affecting more than one million Tibetan children who have been separated from their families, language, and heritage. Your implementation of the Law will be evaluated for compliance with standards for the protection of children," they said. "Let us be clear: We will not hold back from speaking out when laws or practices violate fundamental rights, including the rights of individuals living on U.S. soil, children's rights, and religious freedoms. The Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress is detrimental to and attempts to eliminate the unique identities of Tibetans, Uyghurs, and others. Furthermore, this Law appears to be at odds with China's own constitution, 1984 Regional Ethnic Autonomy Law, and international commitments," said Senators Lindsey Graham and Sheldon Whitehouse. title: "China's Colonial Game in Tibet" launches ahead of Tibetan National Uprising Day - Tibet Post International
content: Dharamshala — "China's Colonial Game in Tibet" was launched in Dharamsala on March 6, 2026, a few days before Tibetan Uprising Day on March 10, 2026. This book talks about the independent status of Tibet, His Holiness the Dalai Lama, the reincarnation of the Dalai Lama, the Tibetan cultural genocide, the destruction of the environment, education as a colonial tool under the Chinese Communist government, the Tibetan freedom movement, and Tibetan self-immolations. This book brings together 39 authors, including Professor Samdhong Rinpoche, Sikyong Penpa Tsering, Claude Arpi, Professor Robert Destro, Geshe Lhador, Chemi Lhamo, and was edited by Vijay Kranti, a veteran Indian journalist and long-time supporter of Tibet. It is published by the Centre for Himalayan Asia Studies And Engagement (CHASE) in New Delhi. The book launch took place in the hall of the Tibetan Settlement Office, in Dharamshala, on March 6, 2026. Tibetan activist Tenzin Tsundue moderated the event, and Vijay Kranti spoke about his new book, Tsering Choephel, President of the Tibetan Youth Congress, delivered a speech of thanks. Tibetan journalists and Tibetans around the Dharamshala were present at the press conference. While talking about the book, Vijay Kranti said, "CHASE, in collaboration with Tibetan Youth Congress (TYC) organised about 30 international webinars on various hot issues related to Tibet and China during 2020-2023 period. We focused on some of the best and experienced communicators as our experts who understand these issues and have long experience in reaching out to their audiences. Finally we selected about 15 webinars which were focused on those issues which Tibet supporters have been raising at various international forums and which present the most inhuman and prominent dimensions of China’s colonial games in Tibet." "Our main challenge was to reproduce the spoken presentations of these experts over the audio-visual platform into essay like written words and present it in the form of a book. This way it is our endeavor to present a wholesome narration of all major colonial problems and issues, being faced by the people of Tibet, into a single book," Vijay Kranti explained. He also spoke about the repressive policies faced by Tibetans in Tibet and the Tibetans who have set themselves on fire to demand freedom in Tibet and the return of His Holiness the Dalai Lama. He said, "Unfortunately this silence of governments, international organizations – especially the United Nations -- and the most influential international media houses who claim to be the greatest champions of human rights and freedom of expression, have been perpetually found wanting on what is going on inside China-occupied colonies like Tibet. Almost all of them have failed individually as well as collectively to take any meaningful action against the blatantly inhuman acts of the Chinese regime against its own people as well as its colonial subjects in occupied countries of Tibet, East Turkestan (Ch: ‘Xinjiang’), Southern Mongolia and Hong Kong." "The saddest and most unfortunate part of this game is that while China’s communist masters have been successful in keeping a strong lid on all these developments, the international community has, in effect, chosen to keep its eyes closed and mouth shut against this ongoing crime against the most helpless section of human society. Hence the need for waking up the world’s conscience before it is too late," he added. He further said, "With the help of 39 well informed experts, observers and researchers from across the world, it is our endeavor at Centre for Himalayan Asia Studies and Engagement (CHASE) to present authentic information on these as well as many other aspects of the colonial games being played by China’s communist masters in China’s colonies. This book is the first and the Tibetan installment in this direction. It is our endeavor to present similar studies on China’s other colonies like East Turkestan, S. Mongolia, Hong Kong, Manchuria etc. in near future." "CHASE organised over 30 international webinars on major issues related to Tibet and China. We organized these webinars with the active participation of Tibetan Youth Congress (TYC) which is the largest and true representative of the struggle and aspirations of the people of Tibet – living in exile as well as those living inside Chinese occupied Tibet. We had the privilege of enrolling some of the best known experts and experienced communicators from across the globe who understands these issues deeply. Out of these 30 webinars we have selected 15 which were focused on all those issues related to the denial of human rights to the people of Tibet as a part of the colonial games which the Chinese Communist Party and its leaders have been playing inside Tibet since its occupation in 1951. This collection of essays and presentations covers almost all such issues related to Tibet and China which have been, time and again, raised at various international forums but not followed up to their logical end. This way it has been the endeavor of CHASE to make this book a unique platform which presents a complete, honest and fearless account of all those colonial games which are being played inside occupied Tibet by its Chinese colonial masters," the Vijay Kranti, President of CHASE concluded his talk. Vijay Kranti is a veteran journalist, Tibetologist and photographer. Over past 50 years he has been on the staff of reputed media groups which include India Today, BBC TV, Zee News TV, Aaj Tak TV, DD News, German Radio Deutsche Welle, Radio Voice of America etc. His main focus areas have been Himalayan Buddhist Culture, Tibet, China and J&K. In 1992 he was awarded KK Birla Foundation Fellowship for journalists for his work on Tibet. His study and research on issues related to Tibet and China has received acknowledgement and appreciation at international levels. He is regularly invited to international conferences, seminars, online webinars, TV and Radio shows to speak on these subjects as an expert. Tibet History Independence

title: "Tibet has never been a part of China since ancient times": CTA - Tibet Post International
content: Dharamshala — Central Tibetan Administration (CTA) organised an event to commemorate the 67th National Uprising of Tibet in Dharamshala, on March 10, 2026. Kashag (Cabinet) states, "Tibet has never been a part of China since ancient times and is rather a nation under the illegal occupation of the communist PRC. The fact that the question of Tibet is not an internal affair of China, but rather an unresolved international conflict." Central Tibetan Administration organised the event to commemorate the 67th National Uprising of Tibet in the courtyard of Thekchen Choeling Tsuglakhang, Dharamshala, on March 10, 2026. Dignitaries including Michael Brand, Member of the German Parliament and Parliamentary State Secretary, Germany; Hans-Gert Pöttering, Former President of the European Parliament; Jiří Oberfalzer, Vice President of the Czech Senate; and Juris Vilums, Member of Parliament, Latvia. Brian Joseph, Vice President, National Endowment for Democracy (NED), Cheng Lei, from Australia, Shri R.K Khrimey, National Convenor of Core Group for Tibetan Cause-India, Ms Alice Parma, Italian State parliamentarian, Senator Jiri Dusek, Vice-chairman of the Committee on EU, and Dr Wiebke Winter, Member of Legislative Assembly, Germany. Participants of the Special International Tibet Support Groups Meeting also presented there as special guests and top officals of CTA and Tibetans around the Dharamshala joined the commemoration of the the 67th National Uprising of Tibet. Sikyong Penpa Tsering hoisted of Tibetan National Flag and sang the Tibetan and Indian National Anthem. Then observed a minute of silence as a mark of respect for the Tibetan Martyrs who have sacrificed their lives for the cause of Tibet. March 10 commemoration song sang by the members of the Tibetan Institute of Performing Arts. Then Sikyong read out the statement of Kashag on the the 67th Anniversary of the Tibetan National Uprising Day and he said," Today marks the 67th anniversary of the 1959 Tibetan National Uprising, when Tibetans from all three provinces, monastics and laypeople alike, rose in unison with indomitable courage in Tibet’s capital, Lhasa, to protest the illegal invasion by the People’s Republic of China (PRC) and to safeguard the person of His Holiness the Fourteenth Dalai Lama from imminent threat. On this solemn occasion, the Kashag pays its deepest tribute to all the martyrs who made the ultimate sacrifice for the sake of Tibet, its faith, and its people, and stands in unwavering solidarity with our brothers and sisters inside Tibet, whose resolve to preserve our distinct national identity remains as unyielding as Mount Meru, even in the face of relentless oppression by the government of the PRC. We also express our sincere gratitude to all our distinguished guests present here today for their powerful demonstration of solidarity with the Tibetan people, and to all nations, organizations, and individuals around the world who continue to support the cause of Tibet. " "At present, the government of the PRC is falsely asserting that Tibet and all non-Han nationalities are part of the constructed “Zhonghua Minzu.” It is mobilizing, under the proclaimed mandate of “forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation,” the full machinery of the state to carry out expansive and deeply entrenched policies within Tibet aimed at eradicating both Tibet’s physical environment and its people’s distinct national identity." "The reckless destruction of the Tibetan Plateau, a strategic geographical region also known as the ‘Water Tower of Asia,’ does not merely impact the two billion people who depend on Tibet’s rivers, but also threatens the interests of the entire world in our collective effort to confront the global climate crisis," he added. The statement of the Kashag states, "Tibet has never been a part of China since ancient times and is rather a nation under the illegal occupation of the communist PRC. The fact that the question of Tibet is not an internal affair of China, but rather an unresolved international conflict, has been clearly established in the “Promoting a Resolution to the Tibet-China Dispute Act” enacted by the U.S. government. Regarding the reincarnation of His Holiness the Dalai Lama, the international community, through around 134 formal pronouncements, including legislations, resolutions, and declarations, categorically rejects the PRC’s so-called three conditions put forth in complete disregard for religious tradition and with an abandonment of political morality, and asserts a unified stance of non-recognition whatsoever. Nevertheless, the PRC continues to push its malicious agenda inside China and Tibet. Alongside its intensifying propaganda campaigns, the PRC government is exploiting its state-appointed Panchen Gyaltsen Norbu and a handful of lamas and monks through staged meetings and scripted speeches. It is certain that such orchestrated attempts will never be accepted by anyone, neither now nor at any point in the future. " Khenpo Sonam Tenphel, Speaker of the Tibetan Parliaments-in-Exile read out the statement of the TPiE on the 67th Anniversary of the Tibetan National Uprising Day and he said,"Throughout the period that Tibet has remained under the illegal occupation of China since its armed invasion, the government of China has kept distorting the country’s historical sovereignty with fabricated narratives, sought to corrupt the unique culture of the Tibetan people by adulterating it, used coercion to deprive the people of Tibet of their freedom of religious belief, set out to devastate the territorial and natural environment of Tibet, kept trampling on the human rights of the Tibetan people, shut them up from exercising their freedom of speech, colonized Tibet in the name of economic development and progress, made active efforts to prevent any expression of the oneness of the nationality of the Tibetan people, and disregarded the wishes of the Tibetan people. Apart from these, the ground reality remains that the government of China has thus far never implemented any genuinely intended policy measure which is suited to the needs of the Tibetan people. Rather, it has relied solely on policies of violent reprisal and brutal repression against the people of Tibet. As a result, the Tibetan people, both the old and new generations, have carried out a succession of protest demonstrations in a campaign that began in 1987. In particular, the great Earth-Mouse Year uprising protests carried out simultaneously by the people of all the three traditional provinces of Tibet in 2008, still remain fresh in our minds. Along with that, it is worth noting that since the year 2009, there have been a total of at least 157 incidents in which individual Tibetans in occupied Tibet have carried out protest self-immolations in acts of a non-violent campaign against the government of China. These various types of protests continue to be carried out by the Tibetan people to this day. It is important that the government of China appreciate the enormity of the sacrifices the Tibetan people have been making through those protest campaigns." Above guests addressed the assembly and reaffirmed their support for the Tibetan cause and the fight for freedom and human rights for the Tibetan people. They criticised the Chinese Communist government for violating the human rights of Tibetans, forcing more than a million Tibetan children as young as four into Chinese colonial-style boarding schools, destroying the Tibetan environment, and interfering in the reincarnation of His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama. Tibet Tibetan Uprising Day

title: Majority of Members of the Parliament of Estonia Sign Landmark Statement Supporting Tibet - Tibet Post International
content: Tallinn — A majority of members of the Parliament of Estonia (Riigikogu) have signed a landmark statement in support of Tibet, marking one of the strongest parliamentary expressions of solidarity with the Tibetan people in recent years. "It is an honour to present an important statement —the result of a major effort—bearing the signatures of a majority of the Parliament of Estonia," said Roy Strider, Coordinator of the Tibet Support Group in the Parliament of Estonia. The Parliament of Estonia consists of 101 members, of whom 51—representing a symbolic majority of more than 50 per cent—have signed the statement in support of Tibet. According to Strider, securing the signatures represented a significant challenge, as Parliament is currently in its summer recess. "We hope that our exceptionally strong support for Tibet—and the declaration at the beginning of the statement that Tibet is a historically independent country, forcibly occupied by China—reflects the firm and unwavering stance of the Estonian people, as well as the sense of brotherhood shared between two small nations," he said in a letter to Tibet Post International. The statement was presented to coincide with the birthday of His Holiness the Dalai Lama. "It gives me great pleasure to present this strong statement at the time of His Holiness the Dalai Lama's birthday," Strider added. The statement has also been published on the official website of the Parliament of Estonia. Strider noted that the broad parliamentary support was also influenced by previous visits made by Estonian parliamentary delegations to Dharamshala. "I would also like to emphasise that, to the best of my belief, the numerous expressions of support are partly due to previous successful visits by delegations of Estonian Members of Parliament to Dharamshala," he continued. The parliamentary statement describes Tibet as "a country historically independent and forcefully occupied by the People's Republic of China (PRC)" and expresses strong opposition to China's Law on Ethnic Unity and Progress, which was adopted on 12 March 2026 and entered into force at the beginning of July 2026. The statement states that the legislation threatens Tibetan identity through measures including mandatory Mandarin-language instruction, expanded state surveillance, policies promoting mixed-ethnic communities, and provisions with extraterritorial implications. It also calls for stronger international action, including diplomatic pressure on Beijing, support for the preservation of Tibetan culture and identity, and greater engagement by United Nations mechanisms. Concluding his message, Strider stressed the importance of international solidarity during a period of growing global uncertainty. "These are difficult times for the world, and we must support one another and stand together more than ever before. I believe that, together, we will overcome all the challenges in our path and always see a ray of hope, reason, and cooperation to strive towards." Based on the official statement issued by the Parliament of Estonia, which acknowledges the historical sovereignty of Tibet and calls on the international community to stand up for the people of Tibet. The following are the key demands, recommendations, and requests articulated in the statement: The statement is jointly issued by the Tibet Support Group in the Estonian Parliament and Members of the Parliament of Estonia (Riigikogu). Tibet is described as "a country historically independent and forcefully occupied by the People's Republic of China (PRC)", and its status is characterised as remaining subject to unresolved international conflicts. China's Law on Ethnic Unity and Progress, adopted on 12 March 2026 and effective from the beginning of July 2026, is presented as the central concern of the statement. The law is described as aiming to erase Tibetan identity by introducing extensive political, educational, and social measures affecting local governments, schools, and communities. Mandatory Mandarin Chinese instruction from pre-kindergarten through high school is criticised as a policy that gradually removes the practical use and relevance of the Tibetan language. The promotion of "mutually embedded community environments" is criticised for encouraging mixed-ethnic neighbourhoods that undermine traditional Tibetan communities and cultural continuity.
