content: Dharamshala — US Senators Jeff Merkley and Jim Risch introduce the Assuring the Future of Tibet Act (AFTA) in Senate, on Wednesday. The AFTA would recognise the Central Tibetan Administration (CTA) as the legitimate representative of the Tibetan people, Support the Tibetan people’s right to self-determination, Affirm that resolving the Tibet-China dispute is a U.S. strategic interest and urge the People’s Republic of China (PRC) to address Tibetan aspirations for their distinct identity; Name the Gaden Phodrang Trust the sole authority to recognise Dalai Lamas, ensuring U.S. support endures beyond the 14th Dalai Lama. The Assuring the Future of Tibet Act (AFTA) was introduced by Senators Jeff Merkley (D-OR) and Jim Risch (R-ID), in Senate on August 12, 2026 and co-sponsored by Senators Tim Kaine (D-VA) Todd Young (R-IN), Jacky Rosen (D-NV), and Rick Scott (R-FL). The legislation is the Senate companion to the bill (H.R. 8982) introduced in May 22, 2026 in the House of Representatives by Reps. Jim McGovern (D-MA) and Michael McCaul (R-TX). “Human rights and basic dignity for the people of Tibet cannot be ignored. Our bipartisan bill sends a clear message that the United States will stand with Tibet in its fight for these fundamental freedoms and the promise of tomorrow,” said Merkley. “As long as the People’s Republic of China continues to ignore the rights of Tibet under international law, America will not abandon the Tibetan people.” “The Chinese Communist Party has sought to erase Tibetan culture, religion, and language, among other grievous actions. What Beijing has done to Tibet, they want to do elsewhere to anyone who defies the CCP,” said Risch. “This bill supports the Tibetan people, key partners in pushing back against China’s authoritarianism, and counters China’s malign influence at the United Nations.” AFTA would recognise the Central Tibetan Administration (CTA) as the legitimate representative of the Tibetan people, Support the Tibetan people’s human rights and right to self-determination, Affirm that resolving the Tibet-China dispute is a U.S. strategic interest and urge the People’s Republic of China (PRC) to address Tibetan aspirations for their distinct identity; Name the Gaden Phodrang Trust the sole authority to recognise Dalai Lamas, ensuring U.S. support endures beyond the 14th Dalai Lama, etc. The International Campaign for Tibet welcomes the introduction of the Assuring the Future of Tibet Act (AFTA) (S.5362) in the US Senate, and it's President Tencho Gyatso said, “I thank Senators Merkley and Risch for introducing this vital bill and Senators Kaine, Young, Rosen, and Scott for serving as its original co-sponsors. The International Campaign for Tibet looks forward to working with Congress towards its swift passage." “At a time when China is accelerating its campaign to erase Tibetan identity, this bill sends a powerful message – that America’s support for the Tibetan people, their democratic institutions, and the Tibetan people’s right to determine their own future is unwavering,” she added. The Assuring the Future of Tibet Act would: Recognize the Central Tibetan Administration (CTA) as the legitimate representative of the Tibetan people and the continuity of governance established by the Dalai Lama, and direct the Secretary of State to engage with the Sikyong and designated representatives at the most senior levels; Support the Tibetan people’s human rights and right to self-determination by advocating at the UN for CTA observer status and equal access across the UN system; Build international recognition of the CTA by pressing for its inclusion in relevant international bodies and organizing like-minded partners and allies behind that effort; Elevate the Sikyong’s standing by extending appropriate diplomatic courtesies, including security consistent with that afforded to a head of government, and considering privileges and immunities for CTA officials; Affirm that resolving the Tibet-China dispute is a U.S. strategic interest and urge the People’s Republic of China (PRC) to address Tibetan aspirations for their distinct identity; Name the Gaden Phodrang Trust the sole authority to recognize Dalai Lamas, ensuring U.S. support endures beyond the 14th Dalai Lama; and Require a report to Congress on implementation, which may be consolidated into existing State Department reporting. Tibet Freedom USA AFTA

title: 151 Tibet Groups call on Foreign Ministers of countries to reject China’s Assimilation Law
content: Dharamshala — 151 Tibetan groups call on the Foreign Ministers of Argentina, Brazil,Canada,France, Germany, India, Italy, Japan, Mexico, Sweden, UK, USA, Vice-President of the European Commission and High Representative of the European Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy to reject the China’s Assimilation Law. China’s new law marks a dangerous new escalation in Beijing’s campaign to erase the distinct identity of the Tibetan people. Behind the language of “unity” lies a powerful legal framework through which Tibetans can be punished for exercising fundamental rights. The Tibet groups addressed to His Excellency Pablo Quirno Magrane, Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Trade and Worship of Argentina; Senator The Ho,. Penny Wong, Australian Minister for Foreign Affairs; His Excellency Mauro Vieira, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Brazil; The Hon. Anita Anand, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Canada; His Excellency Jean-Noël Barrot, Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs of France; His Excellency Dr. Johann Wadephul, Federal Minister for Foreign Affairs of Germany; His Excellency Dr. Subrahmanyam Jaishankar, Minister of External Affairs of the Republic of India; His Excellency Antonio Tajani, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Italy; His Excellency Toshimitsu Motegi, Minister for Foreign Affairs of Japan; His Excellency Roberto Velasco Álvarez, Secretary of Foreign Affairs of Mexico; Her Excellency Maria Malmer Stenergard, Minister for Foreign Affairs of Sweden; The Rt Hon. Yvette Cooper MP, Secretary of State for Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Affairs of the United Kingdom; The Hon. Marco Rubio, Secretary of State of the United States of America; Her Excellency Kaja Kallas, Vice-President of the European Commission and High Representative of the European Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy. They wrote," As China’s “Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress” enters into force on July 1, 2026, we, on behalf of a coalition of 151 Tibet groups and supporters worldwide, condemn this law as a direct assault on the fundamental rights, identity, and future of the Tibetan people." The Tibet groups said, "China’s new law marks a dangerous new escalation in Beijing’s campaign to erase the distinct identity of the Tibetan people. Behind the language of “unity” lies a powerful legal framework through which Tibetans can be punished for exercising fundamental rights: speaking their language, practising their religion, preserving their culture, and peacefully expressing their identity. It is the codification of policies that strike at the heart of Tibetan survival as a distinct people." "The law prioritises Mandarin Chinese in education and public life, mandates state-directed social integration, and expands penalties for alleged threats to “ethnic unity.” Article 20 of the law requires parents to educate children to “love the Communist Party of China” and prohibits the transmission of ideas deemed harmful to national unity. This grants Beijing unprecedented authority to regulate what Tibetan families teach their children about their history, culture, religion, and identity, while deepening systems of ideological control and social surveillance," they added. "For years, China has implemented a vast colonial boarding school system that has removed at least one million Tibetan children from their families and communities. In these “schools,” Tibetan children are subjected to systematic cultural erasure. They are educated primarily in Chinese, denied meaningful access to their mother tongue, restricted from practising their religion, and subjected to intensive political indoctrination designed to reshape their identity and allegiance. Reports and broadcasts show Tibetan schoolchildren participating in military-style drills, patriotic ceremonies and “red education” programmes to cultivate loyalty to Xi Jinping, the Communist Party and the People’s Liberation Army. Disturbing images show children dressed in military fatigues, marching in formation and receiving instruction from military veterans in schools and kindergartens," the 151 groups explained. UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk has sounded the alarm: “I am very concerned about China’s counterterrorism and assimilation policies, particularly as they affect minorities in the Xinjiang, Inner Mongolia and Tibetan regions. The new law on ethnic unity risks deepening restrictions on freedoms of language, education, practice of religion, culture, expression and assembly; and penalizing the peaceful exercise of minority rights in general. I call for the law to be repealed and for these practices to end.” The 151 Tibetan organisations said, "Governments must now join this call for repeal. As your country’s Foreign Minister, you carry a moral, legal, and political responsibility to oppose a law that will accelerate the erosion of Tibetan language, culture, religion, and identity. Silence in the face of this assault on a people’s language, culture, religion, and identity will be remembered as acquiescence." "Together, your governments are uniquely positioned to exercise strong and direct influence over China’s leadership. By acting in unison, you will not only strengthen your leverage with Beijing, but also ensure that participating governments are better protected against efforts to export authoritarian influence into our own democracies. We urge you to act now; collectively, decisively, and without delay," they said. Tibet CCP Tibetans

title: International - Tibet Post International
content: Dharamshala — Addressing the opening of the 63rd session of the United Nations Human Rights Council in Geneva, on September 7, 2026, the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk expressed deep concern over the deteriorating human rights situation in Tibet, particularly restrictions affecting the Tibetan people’s freedom of religion.

title: China has no right to interfere in the choice of the Dalai Lama's reincarnation: Chinese dissidents
content: Dharamshala — The Democratic China and Future of Tibet Forum concluded in Dharamsala with a five-pont declaration. It states, " the declaration addressed independent Chinese perspectives on the reincarnation of His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama. Participants unanimously confirmed that His Holiness the Dalai Lama and his Gaden Phodrang Trust designed by him has the final authority on the reincarnation and the Chinese authorities have no right to interfere, intervene or participate on this matter." The three-day Democratic China and Future of Tibet Forum concluded in Dharamsala, on September 2, 2026 with five key declarations. The forum brought 29 Tibetan and journalists, translators, Chinese study scholars, experts and human rights activists from India, United States, Canada, United Kingdom, Germany, Netherlands, Australia, Japan, Taiwan, and Southern Mongolia. The conferejce wa organised by the Tibetan Community Development Fund (TCDF) in collaboration with the Tibet Policy Institute (TPI), from August 31 to September 2, 2026. The Forum was inaugurated by Sikyong Penpa Tsering of Central Tibetan Administration, on August 3, 2026 and he delivered the keynote address on issues including Sino-Tibetan relations, the Middle Way Approach, the reincarnation of His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama and the importance of cooperation between Tibetans and Chinese. They issued a five-pont declaration and one point states," the declaration addressed independent Chinese perspectives on the reincarnation of His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama. Participants unanimously confirmed that His Holiness the Dalai Lama and his Gaden Phodrang Trust designed by him has the final authority on the reincarnation and the Chinese authorities have no right to interfere, intervene or participate on this matter. The another point states,"declaration examined China’s Law on the Promotion of Ethnic Unity and Progress from a legal and human rights perspective. Participants expressed serious concerns about its potential implications for the languages, cultures and identities of Tibetans, Uyghurs, Southern Mongolians and other ethnic communities, and called for the repeal of the law." One of the declaration reaffirmed nonviolence as a common fundamental principle. "Participants emphasised the importance of peaceful, practical and dialogical approaches to resolving the Sino-Tibetan conflict and recognised nonviolent resistance as a shared principle connecting the Tibetan and Chinese democratic movements," it stated. The declaration also called for developing a common vision for a democratic future. "Participants highlighted the importance of exchanges between Tibetans in exile and Chinese democracy organisations and individuals, promoting the democratic experience of the Tibetan community in exile, and supporting the broader process of democratization in China," the declaration stated. The declaration further focused on deepening understanding of Tibetan democracy, history, Tibetan-Chinese exchanges and the Middle Way Approach. "The forum provided an opportunity for Chinese participants to learn about the Tibetan democratic system and Tibetan perspectives on history, while Tibetans gained greater insight into the Chinese democracy movement. Discussions also examined the Middle Way Approach and its relevance to a peaceful resolution of the Sino-Tibetan conflict," it mentioned. The final day of the forum, the participants attended the Tibetan Democracy Day celebration at the Tibetan Main Temple, Dharamshala, on September 2, 2026. On behalf of the Chinese participants, Wang Dan delivered a speech and the Speaker of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile, Dolma Tsering Tekhang, launched of the book The Chinese Authorities Have No Right to Interfere on the Reincarnation of the Dalai Lama , a compilation of articles written by Chinese scholars and writers. Tibet China Democracy

title: 91st birthday of His Holiness the Dalai Lama celebrates in Leh, Ladakh
content: Leh — 91st birthday of His Holiness the Dalai Lama celebrated at the Shewatsel Teaching Ground in Leh, Ladakh, India on July 6, 2026. Which is organised by the Ladakh Buddhist Association, the All Ladakh Gonpa Association and the Central Tibetan Administration. Thousands of people from all over the world—believers of various faiths, people of diverse ethnic backgrounds, and many others joyfully celebrated his 91st birthday. Upon the arrival of His Holiness the Dalai Lama at the Shewatsel teaching site in Leh, Ladakh, students from TCV Ladakh, along with Tibetan and Ladakhi artists, performed welcome dances. Once he was settled in, His Holiness was presented with a birthday cake made with Tibetan cheese; he ate a slice, and those present wished him a very happy birthday. Next, Chering Dorjay Lakrook, President of the Ladakh Buddhist Association (LBA), delivered a speech at the gathering, followed by Sikyong Penpa Tsering of the Central Tibetan Administration and Dolma Tsering, Speaker of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile (TPiE). Chering Dorjay addressed the gathering, "I prostrate to the Buddha Gautama who, moved by compassion, gave us the teachings to rid us of all wrong views. I greet His Holiness, whose name is Jetsun Jamphel Ngawang Lobsang Yeshé Tenzin Gyatso. Today, everyone in the audience has gathered to celebrate His Holiness’s 91st birthday. On this occasion, on behalf of the LBA, and Tibetans living in Ladakh, I greet His Holiness the Dalai Lama and wish him a ‘Happy Birthday’. It is our good fortune to have him here among us. I pray that he lives a long and healthy life and that all his wishes may be fulfilled." Sikyong said, "Today, as humanity continues to witness one man-made conflict after another, alongside an increasing number of natural disasters and humanitarian crises, the most effective antidote lies in cultivating the seeds of compassion within the human heart and nurturing ethical values in everyday life. In a world confronted by division, violence, and suffering, the timeless message of compassion championed by His Holiness is more relevant and necessary than ever before. Therefore, the Year of Compassion should not be regarded merely as a one-year campaign that concludes after twelve months. Rather, it should serve as the beginning of a lifelong commitment to fostering compassion, kindness, and ethical conduct. Starting within our own families and extending to our communities and society at large, each of us should strive to practice these values every day, every month, every year, and throughout the course of our lives." Speaker of Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile said, "On behalf of all Tibetans in Tibet and in exile, the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile wishes to express immense joy, devotion, and delight in offering heartfelt and sincere greetings and felicitations to His Holiness the Great 14th Dalai Lama, on the auspicious day of his attaining 91 years of age." "On the day after the government of China began implementing on 1 July 2026 its so-called Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress, a patriotic Tibetan hero named Lobsang Palden, also known as Rangzen Loga, a resident of New York City, took a Tibetan national flag on the square in front of the United Nations Headquarters and planted it on a crossroad there. He also distributed placards with slogans such as “China Out of Tibet” written on them. He then set himself on fire in protest against the variety of policies being implemented by the Chinese government directed at the destruction of Tibet as we knew it," the statement of TPiE said. Then His Holiness the Dalai Lama addressed the gathering and said,“Today, here in Ladakh, people have unwavering faith, devotion and strong spiritual bonds. Many people from around the world have also gathered here. You have been praying that I will live long, and from my side I pray: Wherever the Buddha's teaching has not spread, And wherever it has spread but has declined, May I, moved by great compassion, clearly elucidate, This treasury of excellent benefit and happiness for all. "There are people in the world who have no spiritual belief. When I went to China in 1954-55, Mao Zedong told me that religion was like opium. However, practice of the Dharma is not just about propitiating deities and saying prayers. It’s actually about transforming your mind and turning your mind towards the practice of virtue. The significance of the practice of Dharma is to have a calm mind, to train the mind," he added. His Holiness said,“As soon as I wake up, I reflect on bodhichitta, the altruistic awakening mind, as well as the insight into emptiness. Wherever I go, I have a warm heart and I encourage others to cultivate it too. I try to spread warm-heartedness among other people. ‘May I, moved by compassion, illuminate this treasure linked to happiness, well-being and benefit." "I am 91, but according to indications in my dreams it seems I may yet live to be 130. So, I hope to be able to help Chinese people through the teaching of the Buddha and also to help people around the world to lead good, positive lives. This is what I aspire to do — thank you," His Holiness concluded. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te, U.S. Under Secretary of State and Special Coordinator for Tibetan Issues Riley Barnes, as well as the Chief Ministers of several Indian states—notably Pema Khandu (Arunachal), Prem Singh Tamang (Sikkim), Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu (Himachal), Yumnam Khemchand Singh (Manipur), and Mohan Charan Majhi (Odisha)—alongside central government ministers and parliamentarians, extended their warm birthday wishes to His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama on the occasion of his 91st birthday. Tibet Dalai Lama

title: Mass Protest in Chandigarh: Over 500 Tibetans Rally Against Chinese Genocide Law
content: Dharamshala — Over 500 Tibetans from various places in North India gathered in Chandigarh, to protest and denounce China's Genocide law (Ethnic Unity Law), implementing in Tibet, which aims to eliminate Tibetan identity, culture, language, and religion. They further paid tribute to 171 Tibetan martyrs, who sacrificed their lives for a free Tibet, including Pawo Lobga Rangzen and urged United Nations to break its silence on Tibet and hold Beijing accountable for ongoing cultural genocide in Tibet. Over 500 Tibetans from Dehradun (Dekyiling), Delhi, Solan, Manali, Chandra and Paonta Sahib in Himachal Pradesh gathered in Chandigarh for a sweeping mass protest, on August 10, 2026. Which was rganised by Regional TIbetan Youth Congress Paonta Sahib and the Regional Tibetan Women's Association, protestors marched to Panjab University and held a candlelight vigil in Sector 17 to denounce China's Genocide law (Ethnic Unity Law). The demonstration further paid tribute to 171 Tibetan martyrs, who sacrificed their lives for a free Tibet, including Pawo Lobga Rangzen following his recent self-immolation outside the UN Headquarters. In a moving display of defiance and solidarity with compatriots suffering inside Chinese occupied Tibet, 30 individuals—including an Indian supporter—shaved their heads. On July 2, 2026, Tibetan martyr Lobga Rangzen set himself on fire outside the United Nations Headquarters in New York to protest the Chinese government’s repressive policies and laws, including so-called the “Ethnic Unity law,” and demand freedom and independence for Tibet. Since then, Tibetans around the world have launched various protests against the Chinese government’s implementation of the so-called “Law on Ethnic Unity” and other oppressive policies in Tibet. The Tibetan diaspora continues to urge international governments and the United Nations to break their silence and hold Beijing accountable for ongoing cultural genocide in Tibet. Tibet UNHRC Free Tibet

title: RTYC Kalimpong Activists Conclude Peace March to Honour Tibetan Martyr Lobga Rangzen
content: Dharamshala — Seven Tibetan activists, including an 82-year-old elder, successfully concluded their peace march in Salugara, on Thursday. The march was held to honor the memory of Tibetan martyr Lobga Rangzen and demand justice for his ultimate sacrifice. Additionally, the marchers sought to voice their strong protest against China's controversial "Ethnic Unity and Progress Law" and condemn President Xi Jinping’s oppressive policies in Tibet ahead of his anticipated visit to India. As they journeyed along the streets, the activists distributed more than 300 pamphlets outlining their three core demands. To ensure their message reached everyone, they also took the time to verbally explain the aims of the peace march to those who could not read, successfully raising vital awareness about the critical situation inside Tibet and the broader Tibetan cause. The 68-kilometer peace march undertaken by seven Tibetan activists successfully concluded at the Kalchakra Monastery in Salugara, on September 3, 2026. The march commenced in Kalimpong on September 2 to mark the exact two-month anniversary of the passing of Tibetan martyr Lobga Rangzen. The participants included 82-year-old Pema Dhundup, 48-year-old Thinley Choden, 31-year-old Nawang Tsundu, alongside Tashi Dhondup, Lhundup Chonden, Leksang Phengay, and Tenzin Jamphel. The Tibetan martyr Lobga Rangzen—who died on July 2, 2026, after self-immolating in front of the United Nations headquarters in New York to denounce the China's repressive laws and assimilation policies in Tibet (notably the "Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress") and demanded freedom in Tibet and the restoration of Tibet's independence—it is fitting to recall that he became the 171st known Tibetan to self-immolate in a call for freedom for Tibet and the return of His Holiness the Dalai Lama to Tibet. The executive members of RTYC demanded justice for Pawo Lobga Rangzen, who died outside the UN Headquarters during a protest calling on the UN to bring freedom and justice to the Tibetan people. His sacrifice highlighted the severe human rights violations in Tibet and the denial of basic freedom of expression. Activists also urged the international community to honor the justice sought by the 157 known self-immolators inside Tibet, who gave their lives demanding Tibetan freedom and the return of His Holiness the Dalai Lama. They said,"we condemn China’s newly implemented so-called "Ethnic Unity and Progress Law", the aimed at suppressing Tibetan identity, culture, language and freedom." The National People's Congress (NPC) passed a law titled “ Promotion of Ethnic Unity and Progress ”, on March 12, 2026. This law reinforces policies of “Sinicization” and “assimilation,” particularly with regard to Tibetans and other oppressed peoples of Mongolia and East Turkestan. It mandates the Sinicization and assimilation of the Tibetan people, using parents, monasteries, various social organizations, and state institutions as instruments of implementation; the law officially took effect on July 1, 2026. The new law aims to codify Xi Jinping’s policy on ethnic affairs, which promotes greater integration and cultural assimilation under the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) regime. It prioritizes the use of Mandarin in education, public services, and public life, thereby replacing previous policies that allowed instruction in minority languages such as Tibetan, Uyghur, and Mongolian. It also requires religious practices to align with Han-centered Chinese cultural norms and socialist values through the “Sinicization” of religion. U.S Senator Jacky Rosen,Jeff Merkley, John Curtis, and Jim Banks, introduced a Bipartisan Resolution on the China's “Ethnic Unity and Progress Law” in US Senate on June 24, 2026. The resolution condemns China’s "Ethnic Unity and Progress Law," which entered into force on 1 July 2026, and calls on Beijing to end abuses against ethnic and religious minorities, as well as campaigns of transnational repression affecting people in the United States. UN human rights bodies have expressed serious concerns regarding the “Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress" of PRC. They said, “we observe that the newly adopted Law risks restricting the freedom of expression, the right to take part in cultural life, freedom of religion and belief, the rights of persons belonging to various communities, particularly children, to use their own language and conduct their own cultural practices, the right of all persons to quality education and training that fully respect their cultural identity, academic and artistic freedoms, and the right to freedom of assembly and association, as protected under international human rights treaties.” The Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile condemned China’s so-called “Law on Ethnic Unity and Progress” and stated: “Lasting peace cannot be achieved through forced assimilation. Lasting unity cannot be built by erasing identity. ” It further urged the international community to closely monitor this law, express concerns about it, and pressure China to engage in peaceful dialogue to resolve the Sino-Tibetan issue, adding: “Tibet’s future must be built through dialogue, not assimilation; through justice, not coercion.” Sikyong Penpa Tsering said, "The Chinese Communist government’s so-called “Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress,” which took effect on July 1, demands a firm and appropriate response. The legislation includes severe restrictions on the Tibetan language; the falsification of history and identity; forced cultural assimilation at the grassroots level; the Sinicisation of Tibetan Buddhism; enforced ethnic integration; pervasive technological surveillance; political and social coercion; the political vetting of Tibetan cadres; the violation of regional autonomy rights; and the assertion of extraterritorial jurisdiction targeting organisations and individuals worldwide." Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected to visit New Delhi, India, to attend the 18th BRICS Summit scheduled for September 12–13, 2026. The Tibetan activists said," Xi Jinping, you are not welcome to India," directly to protest the Chinese government's forced cultural assimilation, intensive surveillance, and severe restrictions on the religious and basic freedom of expression of the Tibetan people inside Tibet and to protest against the law recently implemented by China—known as the "Ethnic Unity and Progress law"—which aims to eradicate Tibetan language, culture, religion, and identity, and which also targets those fighting for their people's freedom and human rights under Chinese occupation. Tibet Freedom China Justice

title: Communiques - Tibet Post International
content: London – Historically important documents relating to the history of Tibet from the archive of Sir Basil Gould, the former British Political Officer in Sikkim, have been donated by the family to the people of Tibet. This follows the auction of the Sir Basil Gould Collection at Bonhams on 5 June in London.

title: A Tibetan activist begins his peace march for Tibet’s independence
content: Dharamshala — Tibetan activist Tsering Tharchin began his peace march for Tibet’s independence titled as, "Rangzen Yatra" from Dharamshala to New Delhi on Thursday. It is to pay tribute to Tibetan martyr Lobga Rangzen , who self-immolated outside the United Nations headquarters in New York, on July 2, to protest against China's colonial rule in Tibet. It also aims to draw attention from people and the government of India, international governments and NGOs on the critical issues facing by Tibetan people inside the Tibet, under the Chinese occupation. Tsering Tharchin, a Tibetan activist and member of the Regional Tibetan Youth Congress Dharamshala began his peace march titled “Rangzen Yatra” on August 20, 2026 from Dharamshala. The "Rangzen Yatra or Azad Yatra" launched by Sikyong Penpa Tsering, Central Tibetan Administration, at the Police Ground, following mass peach march from McLeod Ganj to Dharamshala by over 5000 Tibetans and Tibet supporters including foreigners and Indians. Tharchin will march through Kangra, Amb, Una, Mohali, Panchkula, Chandigarh, Ambala, Karnal and Sonipat on his way to Delhi. He stated that he would distribute leaflets about Tibet to the Indian public along the way to raise their awareness of the Tibetan issue; he would also meet with leaders and members of parliament to urge them to support the Tibetan issue and stand with the Tibetans. If conditions permit, he will also hold a press conference. Tharchen said, "This Rangzen Yatra is a tribute to Tibetan martyr Lobga Rangzen, who self-immolated outside the United Nations headquarters in New York on July 2, 2026, to protest against China's colonial rule in Tibet, and to all the martyrs who have sacrificed their precious lives for Tibetan freedom and dignity. "Through this march, I want to draw the kind attention of the people and the Government of India, international governments and NGOs and peace loving people to the life-and-death situation of Tibet under Chinese occupation. As a record, In seventy-six years of Chinese occupation of Tibet, China killed more than a million Tibetans, destroyed over 6,000 monasteries, looted millions of dollars worth of Tibetan wealth including priceless treasures and natural resources to feed Chinese industries. It also dammed and diverted Tibetan rivers for industries and data centres in China. "Since Xi Jinping came to power, the level of repression in Tibet has been intensified. China has pursued policies aimed at eradicating Tibetan identity by forcefully assimilating Tibetans especially children into Chinese culture. For example, policies such as the Sinicisation of Tibetan Buddhism and expansion of colonial-style boarding schools and the so-called 'Ethnic Unity Law' are nothing but a death sentence to Tibetans as a distinct people. Such policies are intentionally made to systematically erase Tibetan language, culture and identity in order to solidify Chinese colonial rule in Tibet. It criminalizes the promotion of Tibetan culture in our homeland. This is genocide. "Under these increasingly repressive circumstances in Tibet, His Holiness the Dalai Lama and the Tibetan Government in Exile remain the sole legitimate institutions to represent and safeguard the identity, dignity, and fundamental interests of the Tibetan people. "Tibet is not only a Tibetan issue as it concerns freedom and justice over occupation and genocide. Everybody has an interest and stake in it, especially India. Therefore, through this march, I want to highlight these three important issues: 1. I am urging the international community, governments, organisations and people around the world to recognise the Tibetan Government-in-Exile (Central Tibetan Administration) as the legitimate and true representative of the Tibetan people, and to recognise Tibet as a historically independent nation under Chinese occupation. 2. Tibet historically has been a buffer between India and China. However, China's occupation and militarisation of Tibet, has not only changed it but also created unnecessary geopolitical conflicts including war and military aggressions against India. China has been using Tibet as a strategic platform to undermine India's security and development despite India's attempt to live in peace with China. By exploiting Tibet's historical and cultural ties with some regions in India like Ladakh and Arunachal, China makes illegal claims on Indian territories. The Tibet issue is not merely a matter of Tibetan freedom, but also one that is directly connected to India's national security and development. India has to spend the largest chunk of its defence budget to defend against threats from China and China-supported-Pakistan. 3. Rampant mining, large-scale dam construction, and river-diversion projects across Tibet's fragile ecosystem are causing profound environmental disruption, with consequences extending far beyond the Tibetan plateau. Such destructive activities disturb the ecological balance across the Himalayan region. Over the past decades, we have witnessed increasingly frequent and devastating climate-related disasters such as floods across the Himalayas. Through this campaign, I urge the international community to recognise Tibet's critical ecological importance and take meaningful action to protect its environment, rivers, glaciers, and fragile ecosystems from destructive and unsustainable exploitation in the name of development. Tibet Independence Rangzen

title: China expels Tibetan monks and nuns from Larung Gar and demolished their dwellings
content: Dharamshala — Chinese authorities expelled Tibetan monks and nuns from the Larung Gar, in Sertar County, eastern Tibet, following a large-scale operation to demolish their living quarters that began on July 13, 2026. Furthermore, the authorities are imposing severe restrictions on the freedom of movement of monks and nuns, as well as on pilgrims and tourists to visit to the monastery. The demolitions took place following the implementation of China’s new law, so-called the “Law on Ethnic Unity and Progress.” According to the sources, Chinese authorities in Sertar County, eastern Tibet, recently issued a directive ordering monks and nuns from the Larung Five Sciences Buddhist Academy, better known as Larung Gar (Monastery), whose living quarters had been demolished from July 13 till now, to return to their homes or original monasteries, thereby forbidding them from the monastery and continue their studies. This is a ploy by Chinese authorities to expel these religious practitioners from the monastery under the pretext of demolishing their dwellings. The Chinese authorities announced that the demolition targeted at least 1,060 housing units occupied by monks and nuns; consequently, more than 1060 monastics will be expelled from the monastery, marking a further violation of the religious freedom of Tibetan monks and nuns. In additonally, the Chinese authorities imposed severe restrictions on the freedom of movement of monks and nuns, as well as on pilgrims and tourists to visit to the monastery. The Chinese authorities have demolished thousands of residences of Tibetan monks and nuns in Larung Gar, the world’s largest Tibetan Buddhist institute, since 2001. The latest wave of demolitions began in mid-July and is set to destroy 1,060 dwellings of monks and nuns. These demolitions took place following the implementation of China’s new law, so-called the “Law on Ethnic Unity and Progress,” which came into effect on July 1, 2026. Chinese authorities began to demolish at least 1,060 dwellings belonging to monks and nuns at the Larung Five Sciences Buddhist Academy, starting on July 13, 2026; at least six dwellings were demolished till July 15, 2026. These actions occurred following the implementation of so-called China's new “Law on Ethnic Unity and Progress” on July 1, 2026, which targets the Tibetan language, identity, culture, and religion as part of a policy of Sinicization and imposes the assimilation of Tibetans into Chinese culture through public institutions. "The demolitions in Larung Gar began around July 13, 2026, and are being carried out at night, which is seen as a tactic by the authorities to prevent public documentation, media coverage, and satellite monitoring. As of July 15, 2026, six dwellings had been demolished, and Chinese authorities continue to destroy the residences; they have targeted at least 1,060 dwellings belonging to monks and nuns for demolition as part of this latest phase of demolitions," the sources said. In 2001, Chinese authorities launched their first large-scale demolition and forced eviction operations at the Larung Gar Buddhist Academy, targeting thousands of monastic dwellings. Since then, the Chinese government has intermittently resumed its destruction activities, notably launching a massive demolition operation in July 2016 that reportedly resulted in the expulsion of more than 4,800 monks and nuns and the demolition of 4,700 dwellings. China-Tibet: The one-thing you need to know: Over the past 70 decades, there has been ongoing political repression, social discrimination, economic marginalization, environmental destruction, and cultural assimilation, particularly due to Chinese migration to Tibet which is fueling intense resentment among the people of occupied Tibet. The communist-totalitarian state of China began its invasion of Tibet in 1949, reaching complete occupation of the country in 1959. Since that time, more than 1.2 million people, 20% of the nation's population of six million, have died as a direct result of China's invasion and occupation. In addition, over 99% of Tibet's six thousand religious monasteries, temples, and shrines, have been looted or decimated resulting in the destruction of hundreds of thousands of sacred Buddhist scriptures. Until 1949, Tibet was an independent Buddhist nation in the Himalayas which had little contact with the rest of the world. It existed as a rich cultural storehouse of the Mahayana and Vajrayana teachings of Buddhism. Religion was a unifying theme among the Tibetans -- as was their own language, literature, art, and world view developed by living at high altitudes, under harsh conditions, in a balance with their environment. Tibet Religion Larung Gar

title: Why China is concealing the truth about the devastating floods in Kyirong, Tibet ?
content: Dharamshala — The devastating floods struck Kyirong County and Rasuwa District suddenly and without warning on August 26, 2026. While the human toll in Nepal rises daily, Chinese state media reported an increase in the death count from three to sixteen as of yesterday. How is this possible? Yet, early videos showed hundreds of people being swept away by the flood at the Kyirong port and in other areas in Kyirong. This is their way of concealing the truth by preventing international journalists , scientists, and independent researchers from investigating the real causes of these deadly floods—just as China did during the Dingri earthquake and the COVID-19 pandemic. To date, these catastrophic floods have claimed the lives of 903 people and left more than 4,000 others missing on the Nepalese side; meanwhile, Chinese state media reported 16 confirmed deaths and 546 people affected as of August 30, 2026. However, these figures are hard to believe: while videos initially circulating on Chinese social media showed numerous people and homes struck by the devastating floods, Chinese authorities subsequently removed images of the disaster and calls for help from Tibet, with state media focusing exclusively on rescue teams. However, the reality is cruel, and it is impossible to reveal the true situation in Tibet. On the evening of the flood (August 26), a Tibetan woman living in Nepal called her relatives in Kyirong District to check on them; what she learned broke her heart. A relative explained that the situation was dire: a family member had gone to the site to identify a loved one who had died in the flood, but upon seeing the body, he suffered a heart attack and died instantly. Subsequently, Chinese authorities forbade families from identifying the missing, instead having the victims' bodies immediately buried or removed. She added: “Hundreds of bodies have arrived in Kyirong from the port and flooded areas, but we are not allowed to identify our relatives. Many of them work in and around the ports.” (This conversation took place before the internet was censored in Tibet by Chinese athorities.) This is proof that China is lying to the entire world by censoring the Internet and international journalists, and by preventing local Tibetans from revealing the true situation. A Tibetan woman from Kyirong told Chinese state media that the floods reached them on August 27, 2026; however, this is inaccurate: the waters had already reached Kyirong on the morning of August 26, 2026, even before arriving in Rasuwa, Nepal. By baning international journalists and scientists from visiting the site makes it impossible to determine the true cause of these devastating floods: is the phenomenon linked to glaciers or to dams built by China? Regardless of the origin, China bears responsibility, as it constructs dams, railways, tunnels, and roads there for military purposes, while engaging in activities that accelerate global warming and glacial melting—thereby triggering floods and landslides in Tibet and in neighboring countries such as Nepal and India. "China has aggressively expanded its infrastructure in Tibet (often called "Asia's Water Tower"), with at least 193 hydropower dams built or planned across the region since 2000. These dams span major transboundary river systems, including the upper reaches of the Yangtze, Mekong (Lancang), and Brahmaputra (Yarlung Tsangpo) rivers," according to the International Campaign for Tibet. However, when China builds railway lines, it does not merely construct railway infrastructure; it also conducts mining operations. For instance, during the construction of the Sichuan-Tibet railway line, China severely damaged the environment and stripped the mountains of their mineral resources by excavating hundreds of tunnels. China is also building a trans-Himalayan railway line; the section connecting Lhasa to Kyirong is already complete, and construction of the section linking Kyirong to Kathmandu is set to follow. This project involves tunneling through the fragile Himalayan mountains, which risks triggering further disasters, such as the devastating floods that claimed thousands of lives in Tibet and Nepal. China claiming that there is neither a dam nor a hydroelectric project in Kyirong; however, reports indicate that hundreds of people are stranded at hydroelectric construction sites located between Tibet and the Nepalese border, and that rescue operations are underway to locate more than 900 workers reported missing at these sites. China has claimed that there are no dams in the Kyirong district; however, Chinese state media clearly indicate the existence—since 2013—of the Kyirong Port hydroelectric power station on the Kyirong Tsangpo River. Consequently, the assertion that "there are no dams on the river upstream of Kyirong Port" is factually incorrect. Furthermore, following the 2015 Nepal earthquake, the State Flood Control and Drought Relief Headquarters and the Ministry of Water Resources reported the formation of a landslide-dammed lake located approximately 11 kilometers downstream from the town of Kyirong; Kyirong Port lies just 3 kilometers downstream of this lake. At the time, local residents, border defense troops, and customs personnel were instructed to prepare for evacuation and to take safety measures. Chinese authorities announced today (August 31) that they had taken action and imposed penalty on ten internet users—as part of so-called the "Clean intenet" campaign—for commenting on the flooding at the Kyirong port in Tibet; two other internet users had already been punished on August 26, 2026, according to the China state media (CCTV). This is how China conceals the truth—not only from the people of Tibet and China but also from the rest of the world. One internet user commented, "1,400 people have been affected and over 3,000 people lost their contacts," while another claimed, "Chinese police have confirmed the deaths of 3,000 people." One user commented, "Thousands of people perished in Kyirong," and another wrote, "More than a thousand lives were lost, yet the authorities announced only three." The Chinese government conceals everything happening in Tibet: protests , detentions , arrests, imprisonments, environmental destruction , illegal mining activities, the closure of Tibetan schools , the arrest of intellectuals and teachers. They also prohibited Tibetan children young as four-year old from learning their language, culture and forcibly placed in Chinese boarding schools. The authorities further destroyed monasteries , Buddha statues, and stupas , not to mention the ban on young Tibetans becoming monks. The Chinese government is doing everything in its power to eradicate Tibetan identity and religion. To protest against these oppressive policies in Tibet, a Tibetan independence activist Lobga Rangzen self-immolated in front of UN headquarters in New York, on July 2,2026, to denounce the repressive laws and assimilation policies implemented by China in Tibet, particularly the “Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress”; and demanded freedom and retore independence for Tibet. He became the 171 known Tibetans have set themselves on fire to demand freedom for Tibet and the return of His Holiness the Dalai Lama. As long as China conceals the truth, people will suffer and die; Tibetans constantly repeat, "China lies, people die"—that is the reality. The world is now becoming aware of how the Chinese regime operates and of its expansionism, particularly since the COVID-19 pandemic. While the official death toll from the virus stands at around 7.1 million worldwide, the actual excess mortality is estimated to be far higher—between 18.5 and 35.2 million deaths—because China obscured the truth and prevented international scientists and independent researchers from traveling to Wuhan to determine the virus's origin. Tibet Nepal flood truth

title: China's irresponsible actions are inflicting severe harm on humanity as a whole: Sikyong
content: Dharamshala — Central Tibetan Administration and Tibetans in Dharamshala held a prayer service or the victims and those who lost their lives in the devastating floods that occurred on August 26, 2026, in Kyirong (Tibet) and Rasuwa (Nepal). Sikyong said, "On the Tibetan plateau, the Chinese government has been carrying out various environmentally destructive activities including construction of reservoirs and dams, solar power projects, and railway-linking projects. These irresponsible actions are inflicting severe harm on humanity as a whole. This is not a time to remain silent in the face of circumstances that could lead to even graver dangers ahead." The Central Tibetan Administration held a prayer service at the main Tibetan temple in Dharamsala on August 27, 2026, for the victims and those who lost their lives in the devastating floods that occurred on August 26, 2026, in Kyirong (Tibet) and Rasuwa (Nepal). Top leaders of CTA, all staff and Tibetans around the Dharamshala joined the prayer. His Holiness the 14th Dalai Lama, the Spiritual leader of Tibet, expressed his condolences over devastating floods along the Tibet and Nepal Border. During the prayer service, Penpa Tsering, Sikyong of CTA said," According to information received so far through various news channels and the relevant Tibetan Settlement Office in Nepal, the flash flood that struck the Lha-Dep-Phu (Lhende river) on the Tibet-Nepal border caused major destruction — sweeping away large numbers of homes along the river’s course in Kyirong, Tibet and in Rasuwa district, Nepal. Over 1500 people are reported dead, injured, or missing, resulting in massive devastation. "Footage from security cameras and personal video clips circulating through media channels shows that in a single location- Kyirong (border) Gate alone- the flood swept away houses and hundreds of people in an instant. After concealing the number of casualties for a day, the Chinese government today reported 3 deaths, 558 people missing or unaccounted, of whom approximately 260 are said to be foreign nationals in Tibet — though detailed information remains unclear. "Within the jurisdiction of the Nepal-based Sha-Wa-Ra Sum Tibetan Settlement Office, the Nepalese government has recognised the Shabru settlement, nearby Shabru market, and Timure on the Kyirong border as the areas that suffered the greatest damage from this flood. "In the region, there are five scattered Tibetan settlements/communities: 1. At Rasuwa Gegayling settlement, the flood swept away all 11 households. The two elderly residents who lived there are missing. At Shabru market, 2 homes were completely swept away. Of the residents, 1 person died, and 3 others are missing. 2. At Timure, 2 Tibetan households comprising 6 people are missing. 3. In the areas of Tengpoche, 4. Khangjim, and 5. Briddim, all 6 households are situated on higher ground and hence suffered no damage. "This morning, reports say the Nepalese government had been able to rescue 6 Tibetans. This information is currently being verified. "Nepal has suffered widespread devastation, leaving at least 165 people dead and 826 others missing as of now. "This devastating flood has left a total of more than 1,500 people from Tibet and Nepal dead or missing, including more than 800 foreign nationals affected. "For more than five decades, His Holiness the Dalai Lama has repeatedly issued guidance on the need to protect the global environment in general, and Tibet’s natural environment in particular. Despite the continuous efforts of the Central Tibetan Administration to draw the attention of the international community to Tibet’s environment, only a small number of environmental protection organisations have responded, and it remains rare for the relevant countries to express the necessary degree of concern. "On the Tibetan plateau, the Chinese government has been carrying out various environmentally destructive activities under the pretext of development, causing temperatures to rise at a doubled rate. These days, the Chinese government is openly and relentlessly expanding projects across the Himalayan range, justified as “green” energy sources — including construction of reservoirs and dams, solar power projects, and railway-linking projects. These irresponsible actions are inflicting severe harm on humanity as a whole. This is not a time to remain silent in the face of circumstances that could lead to even graver dangers ahead. "Today, from Ladakh, His Holiness the Dalai Lama offered prayers for those affected by the flood disaster in Tibet and Nepal. His Holiness urged that the region’s natural environment be protected and cared for in ensuring such disasters do not recur in the future. "The Central Tibetan Administration extends its deep condolences and expresses solidarity with all those affected — both living and deceased — by this flood disaster. At this prayer service held today at Thekchen Choeling Temple, we pray for the injured to recover swiftly, the deceased to attain liberation, and the loved ones to be freed from their sufferings. The Central Tibetan Administration has instructed the relevant offices and individuals to carry out emergency relief work without delay. "Likewise, to assist the Central Tibetan Administration’s relief efforts for those affected in the Tibetan residential areas within the Sha-Wa-Ra Sum Tibetan settlement, and to express solidarity and condolences with the government and people of Nepal, we appeal to the Tibetans in exile to make voluntary contributions through their respective Offices of Tibet and the Tibetan Settlement Offices," Sikyong concluded his statement. China Prayers CTA flood

title: Ten cyclists call on the UN to hold China accountable for its genocidal law in Tibet
content: Dharamshala — Ten Tibetan activists undertook a seven-day bicycle journey from Paonta Sahib to Dharamshala, paid tribute to the Tibetan martyr Lobga Rangzen, and expressed their gratitude to the Indian people and government. They also condemned China's newly enacted “Ethnic Unity and Progress Law” and called on the UN and the UN Human Rights Council to take a stand on the case of Lobga Rangzen and to address the critical situation in Tibet. Ten Tibetan activists from the Paonta Sahib Regional Tibetan Youth Congress (RTYC) arrived in Dharamshala on August 19, 2026, after a 171-hour cycling journey that began in Paonta Sahib, Himachal Pradesh. They began their cycle rally on August 13, 2026, from Paonta Sahib and pedaled for seven days, braving hardships, rain, and sunshine, before arriving in Dharamshala today. The cycling rally aims to honor the Tibetan martyr Lobga Rangze n, who sacrificed his life for the just cause of Tibet, to denounce the repressive laws and assimilation policies implemented by China in Tibet, particularly the “Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress”; and to retore independence for Tibet. The rally also condemned the so-called “the “Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress” and demand its repeal. They further called on the UN and the UN Human Rights Council to take a stand on the case of Lobga Rangzen and to address the critical situation in Tibet. Upon their arrival in Dharamsala, the Tibetan Youth Congress held a press conference on August 19, 2026, at the site of the TYC hunger strike front of the Tibetan Market, near the Dalai Lama’s temple in McLeod Ganj, Dharamsala, H.P, India. Ngawang Paljor, President of the Paonta Sahib Regional Tibetan Youth Congress, said: “There are ten cyclists and eight support staff, for a total of 18 Tibetans. The goal of our bike ride is to raise awareness among the general public and Indians in particular about the Tibetan cause. We also held a press conference in Chandigarh and distributed leaflets about the Pawo Lobga Rangzen and the critical situation in Tibet.” When asked what challenges they had faced along the way, he replied, “We didn’t run into any major problems; the sun and the heat were the hardest things to endure during the bike ride. Some of us got sick, but we still managed to reach our destination (Dharamshala).” The President said, “We have three demands. First, we call on the UN and international organisations to hold the Chinese government accountable for implementing repressive policies in Tibet, particularly the “Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress”, as well as for the serious human rights violations committed in the region, including detentions, arrests, acts of torture, and the imprisonment of Tibetans who are merely exercising their fundamental rights to protect their language, their environment, and their faith in their spiritual leaders, notably His Holiness the Dalai Lama. Second, we condemn and reject the so-called ‘Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress.’ Third, we thank the Indian government and people for hosting Tibetans for more than 70 years.” Tibet Human Rights China UNO

title: China and India hold key border issue talks ahead of expected President Xi visit to India
author: tibetanreview
content: (TibetanReview.net, Aug25’26) – India’s National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi have on Aug 25 held the 25th round of Special Representatives’ talks on the India-Tibet boundary question in Beijing ahead of an expected visit to India next month by President Xi Jinping for the BRICS Summit. The talks focused on the boundary question, bilateral relations and regional and international developments, as New Delhi and Beijing seek to consolidate a cautious stabilisation in ties following the prolonged military stand-off in eastern Ladakh triggered by the 2020 Galwan Valley clash, said indiatoday.in Aug 25. The report said the meeting assumed added significance as it took place ahead of the BRICS summit in New Delhi on Sep 12 and 13, which is expected to see participation by Chinese President Xi Jinping, although Beijing has not officially confirmed his visit yet. The visit, should it take place, will be Xi’s first in seven years. A potential meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Xi on the sidelines of the summit could provide political momentum to efforts to improve bilateral relations. The two last met in Aug 2025 on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Tianjin, the report said. The two sides have plenty of issues, including weighty ones, to discuss on their differences as well as scopes for cooperation. To India, one of the most important issues is the situation along its border with Chinese occupied Tibet on which there has been no progress at all on a settlement. Discussions still continue to be focused on maintaining the peace even as the two sides continue to sustain their build-up and remain battle-ready at all times. India has repeatedly maintained that peace and tranquillity along the border are fundamental to the wider relationship. Speaking at the Economic Times World Leaders Forum in New Delhi on Aug 22, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar reiterated that peace and tranquillity in the border areas were a prerequisite for stable relations between the two countries, the report said. NSA Shri Ajit Doval co-chaired the 25th Meeting of SRs on India-China Boundary Question with his counterpart H. E. Wang Yi, Member of the Politburo of the Central Committee of the CPC and China’s Foreign Minister on 25 August 2026 in Beijing. (Photo courtesy: X/India in China) It also cited India’s Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) as describing developments along the border as a matter of the “most serious” concern. Its spokesperson, Randhir Jaiswal, also said recently that maintaining peace and tranquillity along the LAC was of “utmost importance”, stressing that the situation on the frontier would determine the overall trajectory of India-China relations. China, however, continues to give less importance to the border issue, and more on other areas of bilateral ties between the two sides, including especially trade and investment on which it already enjoys huge and growing advantages. The trade balance has continued to balloon in China’s favour despite India’s constant efforts, year after year, to get Beijing to address the increasingly unsustainable imbalance by opening up its markets to Indian products and services. On the border issue, while the disengagement process in eastern Ladakh has helped ease some of the immediate military tensions along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), the broader boundary dispute remains unresolved. Arunachal Pradesh continues to be one of the most sensitive components of the dispute, the report noted. China has enhanced its claims on the entire Indian state of Arunachal Pradesh, which it has taken to refer to as “Zangnan”, or southern Tibet, in recent years. India has consistently rejected the claim, maintaining that the state is an integral and inalienable part of itself. The India-Tibet boundary extends approximately 3,488 km and remains disputed across three broad sectors, with significant differences between the two sides over their respective perceptions of the LAC. While a final settlement still remains a far cry, the two sides have worked out a structured channel for senior-level political communication, particularly during periods when tensions along the frontier have threatened to spill over into the wider relationship. Ahead of the Doval-Wang meeting, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian described the Special Representatives talks as the “main channel” for negotiations between China and India on the boundary question and an important platform for communication on issues of mutual interest. The Aug 25 talks mark the latest high-level diplomatic engagement as both sides seek to maintain that current stabilisation while differences over the boundary remain unresolved, the report said. The Doval-Wang talks could help provide a diplomatic backdrop for high-level engagement between Modi and Xi by addressing sensitive areas of disagreement and reinforcing existing understandings on maintaining peace along the LAC, the report added.

title: China is building a vast ‘national ring road’ uniting the entire PRC borderlands
author: tibetanreview
content: (TibetanReview.net, Aug24’26) – China is building a vast “national ring road”, known as the “border-coast loop”, meant to be a national unity road in the wake of the recent implementation of its national Ethnic Unity Law, encompassing the borders of the entire current territories constituting parts of the People’s Republic of China (PRC). China has outlined plans to build a massive road-link snaking along the PRC’s land borders and coastlines – an ambitious project that could boost incomes in a string of remote regions, but also provoke geopolitical and ecological risks, reported the scmp.com Aug 23. It said the project is framed as an effort to boost economic development, social stability and national unity, with its more than 25,000km (15,500-mile) route set to run through several regions with large ethnic-minority populations – including Tibet and the Xinjiang Uygur autonomous region (East Turkestan). Like the numerous other gargantuan projects China has carried out over the years or is still carrying out, the “border-coast loop” also has to overcome many challenges. Beijing will need to navigate some tricky geopolitical terrain to complete the road, which will run close to areas subject to territorial disputes, while also managing ecological hazards in rugged landscapes with fragile ecosystems, the report noted. One part of the road project – dubbed the “golden border-coast loop” by Chinese state media – is due to be completed by 2030 and will be made up of three sections, the report said, citing a five-year blueprint issued by China’s Ministry of Transport in July. The first section – the G219 highway – runs through the PRC’s southwest and far west, from Guangxi Zhuang autonomous region through Yunnan province and Tibet autonomous region to the northernmost tip of Xinjiang. Stretching 10,000km, the route will closely follow the PRC’s borders with Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, India, Bhutan, Nepal, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Russia, the report said. “This entire transport loop will not only offer the public a fresh road trip experience, but will also unlock tremendous benefits in industrial synergy, border consolidation and border-area stability and development,” the Ministry of Transport was quoted as saying. Beautiful yet remote areas in Tibet, Xinjiang and Inner Mongolia that had long been inaccessible for most tourists would now become easily reachable, it has added. The report said the project also appeared to dovetail with Beijing’s new ethnic unity law, which came into effect in July and signals a shift in policy towards assimilation. * * * But Beijing is likely to run into challenges as it pushes forward with construction. For one thing, the thaw in relations between China and India remains shaky after years of border disputes that at times spilled over into deadly confrontations. India views the G219 highway with concern. In 2024, New Delhi protested the road upgrades and extensions taking place in disputed border areas – part of the preparatory work for the G219 project – which it framed as an attempt by China to alter the facts on the ground in the region, the report noted. Environmental protection is stated to be another concern. In June, a report by China’s Ministry of Ecology and Environment on its key projects for the next five years noted that several areas near the road would require continuous monitoring, including the alpine border regions of Tibet, desert areas in southern Xinjiang, and Tianshan mountains’ glacial regions, the report noted. But despite these challenges, China’s connectivity push is stated to go far beyond the loop project. The country has already built the world’s largest highway and rail networks, which increasingly extend into Tibet and Xinjiang. In August, Beijing established the Xinjiang-Tibet Railway Company to oversee the construction of a 1,980km line running from the Tibetan capital of Lhasa to Hotan in Xinjiang, the report noted. Earlier, in 2022, China unveiled plans for a new highway between Lhunze in southern Tibet and Mazha in Xinjiang, which will also run near areas subject to overlapping claims from Beijing and New Delhi. The road, which will intersect with the G219, is currently under construction, the report said.

title: US envoy concludes Ladakh visit, misses Dalai Lama meeting
author: tibetanreview
content: (TibetanReview.net, Aug23’26) – A strongly anticipated meeting between the US ambassador to India, Sergio Gor, and Tibet’s exiled spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, in the Union Territory of Ladakh did not take place after all. The Dalai Lama has been sojourning in Ladakh since Jun 28 for an extended summer stay while Gor arrived there on Aug 20 after high-profile engagements in neighbouring Jammu and Kashmir (J&K). Gor’s visit was the first by a top US envoy to this strategic frontier region of India since the 2020 Galwan clashes and subsequent border standoff with China. While in J&K, Gor, speaking to reporters alongside Chief Minister Omar Abdullah following their high-level dialogue, remarked, “Kashmir is an important part of India. I am visiting the place for the first time. It is an incredibly beautiful place.” Gor concluded his visit to J&K and Ladakh on Aug 21, after visiting the centuries-old, 12-storeyed Thiksey Monastery, one of the largest and most prominent monasteries in central Ladakh, located about 19km from capital Leh. The monastery is widely noted for its resemblance to the Potala Palace in Tibet’s capital Lhasa. The monastery’s top lama, Thiksey Rinpoche, has regularly welcomed the Dalai Lama during his annual summer visits to Ladakh over the past many years. Gor showed keen interest in Ladakh’s spiritual heritage and cultural traditions. He spent about half an hour visiting the temples and learning about Ladakh’s tradition, Buddhist heritage and more about the place, reported the f reepressjournal.in Aug 22. One of the main attractions there is the Maitreya Temple, which commemorates the visit of the 14th Dalai Lama to this monastery in 1970. It features a 15-metre (49 ft) high statue of Maitreya, the immediate future Buddha, which is the largest such statue in Ladakh, covering two stories of the building., the report noted. Still, the most telling event of Gor’s first trip to Ladakh was a meeting that never took place, said indiatoday.in Aug 21. The Central Tibetan Administration of the exile Tibetans told the media that there was a change in the programme on the night preceding Gor’s visit, and so the meeting did not happen. But neither side has explained why. And in diplomacy, that silence usually says more than a statement would, the report said. At least one comment on X said the decision smacked of pressure from China: “ China ka danda pada lagta hai, ” noted the news outlet FirstPost on its on X account Aug 20. * * * Indeed, the decision may have to do with the fact that Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected to visit the United States in the next two weeks, as revealed by President Donald Trump while addressing a Republican campaign rally in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina, on Aug 21, according to a mid-day.com report Aug 22. Trump did not provide a specific date, venue or agenda for his expected meeting with Xi, the report said. Also, a meeting between the US ambassador and the Dalai Lama, whom Beijing regards as a separatist threat to its rule over Tibet, and that too on Ladakhi soil, would have been read in Beijing as Washington needling China on its most sensitive frontier. Besides, it was something better avoided ahead of a BRICS Summit being hosted by India next month, said the indiatoday.in report. The Kashmir and Ladakh legs of Gor’s trip form one story: an envoy with real proximity to the Oval Office, moving through India’s frontier geographies, saying just enough to please New Delhi, and doing just enough to avoid antagonising Beijing, the report concluded.

title: Report: Tibet repression intensifying as Xi looks to prolong his rule beyond 21st Party Congress in 2027
author: tibetanreview
content: (TibetanReview.net, Aug22’26) – China is cultivating a more repressive leadership in Tibet as it has begun implementing its forced assimilation policy there under the cover of its Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress (Ethnic Unity Law), and ahead of the pivotal 21 st Congress of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) in 2027. As a result, the seventh-generation leadership in Tibet will be shaped by two guiding principles that institutionalize centralized Party control and accelerate Beijing’s forced assimilation of Tibetans – the Ethnic Unity Law and Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building – said Washington-based International Campaign for Tibet (ICT) as it released its 2026 Tibet Leadership Report on Aug 18. Citing leadership appointments, the new legislation, and Party directives, the group says China is deepening political control over Tibet and accelerating its policies of forced assimilation of Tibetans amid a continued lack of any meaningful Tibetan representation in senior leadership positions. The group notes that the Ethnic Unity Law is Beijing’s most significant legal codification of assimilation policies to date, expanding Party authority over education, language, religion and culture while accelerating the shift toward Mandarin-medium education and restricting space for Tibetan identity. Drawing on new leadership data, the report finds that Tibetans remain largely excluded from positions of real political authority, with meaningful decision-making continuing to rest overwhelmingly in the hands of Chinese Party leaders. “As of July 31, 2026, Tibetans hold only 62 of 240 (25.8%) senior leadership positions across provincial, prefectural, and county levels, while non-Tibetans occupy 178 (74.2%). The absence of Tibetans is most pronounced in the Party, security, military, and judicial institutions that exercise the greatest political authority.” Referring to the absence of Tibetans in the higher echelons of the CCP leadership, the report refers to the fact that in the powerful United Front Work Department (UFWD), which oversees Beijing’s Tibet policy, there has not been a Tibetan at the senior leadership level since Sithar (Si Ta) retired as Vice Minister in 2016. In this scenario, the Ethnic Unity Law further weakens the protections nominally guaranteed under China’s regional ethnic autonomy system. Its implementation is expected to accelerate President Xi’s assimilation move and leave future Tibetan leaders with little scope to uphold the autonomous rights guaranteed under the Constitution and the Law on Regional Ethnic Autonomy, the report says. The report says currently, the highest CCP leadership positions in the Tibetan areas are held by non-Tibetans, and there is no indication that Tibetans will assume leadership positions in the coming years. The report notes that in the current, 20th Party Congress, Yan Jinhai (born 1962), former Tibet Autonomous Region (TAR) Chairman and current Chair of the TAR People’s Congress, is the only Tibetan in the CCP Central Committee. Karma Tseten (Chinese: Gama Cedain, born 1967), Phurbu Dhondup (Pubu Dunzhu, born 1972), and Tsering Thar (Cering Tar, born 1969) are the only three ethnic Tibetans in the 171 alternate members of the 20th Party Central Committee. (Based on savetibet.org report Aug 18, 2026)

title: Australian Senator urges targeted sanctions on Chinese leaders enforcing transnational Ethnic Unity Law
author: tibetanreview
content: (TibetanReview.net, Aug22’26) – An Australian Senator has on Aug 20 called for targeted sanctions against Chinese leaders responsible for carrying out transnational repression against Tibetans and others under Beijing’s recently enforced Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress. This law on forced assimilation of Tibetans and other ethnic minority groups in the People’s Republic of China includes provision to punish those, whether within or outside the country, who oppose or criticize its implementation. In his remarks in the Australian Senate, Senator Dean Smith raised concerns about China’s new “Ethnic Unity and Progress Law” and its potential impact on Tibetans living in Australia, said a Tibet.net report Aug 21. Smith, who is the Co-Chair of the Australian Parliamentary Group for Tibet, has said that Australia is home to vibrant Tibetan, Uyghur, Hong Kong and other diaspora communities who come to this country seeking freedom, democracy and the protection of the rule of law. They should never have to fear that exercising those freedoms in Australia could place them or their families overseas at risk. He has expressed alarm that for members of the Australian Tibetan community, simply voting in elections for the Tibetan government in exile, publicly supporting the Dalai Lama, or expressing their cultural and religious identity could potentially be interpreted by Chinese authorities as conduct falling within these sweeping laws. He has therefore called on the Australian Government to recognise transnational repression as a genuine national security threat and to consider targeted sanctions, including Magnitsky-style sanctions, against individuals responsible for organising or directing overseas repression and intimidation. The Magnitsky sanctions programme is a targeted US government initiative used to freeze assets and ban travel for foreign individuals and entities responsible for human rights abuses or major corruption. Named after Russian lawyer Sergei Magnitsky, the framework, initially passed by the Congress in 2012 to target Russia but expanded globally in 2016, provides for penalizing wrongdoers without targeting entire countries. Magnitsky was a Russian tax lawyer who died in a Moscow prison in 2009 after he uncovered a massive, $230 million government corruption scheme.

title: Prayers, protests mark 49th day of Lobga Rangzen’s self-immolation death, and to protest China’s forced assimilation move in Tibet
author: tibetanreview
content: (TibetanReview.net, Aug21’26) – Prayer services as well as peace and protest marches have been held by Tibetan communities and supporters across the free world Over Aug 19-20, marking the end of the seven weeks since Lobsang Palden, better known by his independence-activist name Lobga Rangzen, carried out his protest self-immolation in front of the UN Headquarters in New York city and succumbed to his injuries on Jul 2. The events highlighted China’s current move to forcibly assimilate the Tibetan and other “ethnic minority” peoples through its recently implemented Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress, which Lobga Rangzen had highlighted in his last message, with a call for Tibetan unity to fight for independence. The 49 th day is significant in the Tibetan Buddhist funerary service as the day by which a deceased person is believed to have left their intermediate state for their rebirth. Enlightened beings are believed to determine their own rebirth, although China has sought to upend this by requiring reincarnation of Tibetan Buddhist leaders to be determined only by its atheist leaders’ choices, opening every possibility for making of wrong choices. In Dharamshala, the exile Tibetan headquarters, the Kashag (cabinet) of the Central Tibetan Administration (CTA), and the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile jointly organized a prayer service in the Tsuglakhang, the main Buddhist temple in the area, followed by a peace march from there to the downtown Police Ground, both of which reportedly saw participation by over 5,000 Tibetans. Top exile Tibetan leaders led both those events. The CTA leadership led a 49th‑Day Prayer Ceremony and a Peaceful March in Dharamshala to honour Tibetan martyr Lobga Rangzen. (Photo courtesy: Tibetan Parliamen-in-Exile) On the same day, the Tibetan Youth Congress (TYC), which campaigns for Tibet’s independence, concluded a 33-day relay hunger-strike near the gate of the Tsuglakhang, with the campaign action scheduled to be continued in front of the UN Headquarters in New york City from the following day. The day also saw a Regional TYC group, with 13 participants, from the Tibetan settlement in Poanta Sahib conclude a 360-km bicycle rally in honour of and to pay tribute to Lobga Rangzen for his ultimate sacrifice. The rally was given a rousing reception. The Kashag was also stated to have dispatched instructions to all Tibetan Settlement Offices and Offices of Tibet to organise similar prayer services in their respective regions, ensuring that Tibetans across the world could collectively remember and honour those who had made the ultimate sacrifice for Tibet. Protests were also held in several Indian cities, including New Delhi, Kolkata, Dharamshala, Chennai and Bengaluru, among other centres, with many of the events being addressed by Indian leaders and supporters. * * * “Today marks the 49th day since he passed away. It is the final prayer for him and a day to reaffirm our struggle for freedom against China,” chosun.com Aug 20 quoted a Tibetan attending the “Lobga Rangzen 49th-Day Memorial Service” in New York City as saying. The report cited organizers as saying nearly 1,000 Tibetans from across North America, including New York, New Jersey, Canada, and Europe, had visited the site of Lobga Rangzen’s self-immolation. Colourful flowers and hundreds of candles surrounded an altar set up at the site, with Tibetan monks in maroon robes seated behind them. The low chanting of Buddhist scriptures echoed through Manhattan’s city centre. Above their heads, the Tibetan snow lion flag fluttered in the wind alongside the US flag, the report noted.
